#3833. Bringing Bloodborne back is tricky because "there's a lot of involved rights associated," according to former PlayStation boss

Every year, Bloodborne fans pray for the birth of another game set in FromSoftware's Lovecraftian world. Every year, we're no closer to a Bloodborne 2 or even a Bloodborne Remastered. But why? PlayStation's former head honcho, Shawn Layden, blames it on the tricky situation of rights ownership.

Asked about the noticeable lack of Bloodborne in the decade since its blood moon shone down on us all, in an interview with The Trophy Room podcast, Layden explained that returning to any beloved game is tough.

"Bringing back old games has a certain challenge to it," he said. "Can you do something that is not only respectful of the original, but can you, you know, recreate the phenomenon as it were?"

Bloodborne's situation is slightly more complicated, though. It seems that the rights are somehow split between original publisher PlayStation, developer FromSoftware and the studio's primary stakeholder Kadokawa Corporation.

"There's a lot of involved rights associated with it, and in something like that - where Sony's in there and [FromSoftware] is in there and From's parent company is in there - I think just getting everyone to sign off on the same thing is probably the biggest challenge there," Layden said.

Having led the PlayStation brand during most of its PS4 golden years, Layden said working with FromSoftware on Bloodborne and the original Demon's Souls was "fantastic."

Despite endless calls for a comeback and very stable sales more than a decade on, Bloodborne itself is still stuck on the PS4 - though it's still playable via backward compatibility on the PS5, I should add. The closest we seemingly got to a Bloodborne comeback came from Bluepoint Games, which reportedly pitched a remake sometime before parent company PlayStation shut down the acclaimed studio, though FromSoftware supposedly didn't want the project to go ahead.

Another former PlayStation executive, Shuhei Yoshida, previously speculated that Bloodborne hasn't been remade because game director and soulslike pioneer, Hidetaka Miyazaki, would prefer to handle it himself: "Miyazaki-san really, really loved Bloodborne, what he created… So I think he is interested but he's so successful and he's so busy, so he cannot do it himself, and he doesn't want anyone else to touch it."

Elsewhere, a Bloodborne animated feature is in the works with YouTuber JackSepticEye attached as a co-producer.

#3832. Slay the Spire 2's "biggest" beta patch yet adds its first new early access and foolish character, two game modes, and more tweaks than you can shake a stick at

Hark! A new Slay the Spire 2 patch is here! Or, well, it is if you're someone who's trying out the beta branches of the game. If you're not, it might be worth trying out, as Mega Crit say this is their biggest patch for the game so far, with "some really impactful bits of content that will require lots of testing before they reach the main branch."

First up, a new character: The Fool! "Wah!! The first new character for Early Access arrives!" a Steam blog post explains. "A silly musician who wields a bow! How can such a whimsical creature survive within the Spire? Why, that's up to you! We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch. Even more importantly, be sure to have fun figuring out all the strategies and story of this gently bard. It would be foolish not to!" The post doesn't go into much detail as to what the new character can actually do, so, you'll have to discover that one for yourself!

There are also two new game modes to try out with this beta update. The first is Blitz, a "condensed and chaotic deckbuilding-focused mode." Here, the "Merchant's wares feel a bit off, the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters." You'll also find it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across every character, and you can unlock it by completing an Ascension run on any difficulty. The second mode is Dread, which as the name implies, is a "brutal" difficulty mode that you can only play if you've reached Ascension 10 on every character, including The Fool. "All ascension modifiers are enabled. Bosses are stronger and buff all enemies in their Act. Curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire. Death is expected."

You can expect a bunch of new balance tweaks and changes too. For starters, you'll find that rest sites can now appear a floor earlier every act. New events have been added to Underdocks and Act 2 and 3 too. Some nice quality of life alterations have been made, like how the character select screen for standard runs will start on whatever character you played as last, and controller navigation at the Merchant has been improved too. You can read all about the rest of the many changes right here.

#3831. Mass Effect-like RPG The Expanse: Osiris Reborn ropes in David Gaider, the original lead writer of Bioware's Dragon Age series

"Focusing on certain aspects of the game's narrative."

The Expanse: Osiris Reborn looks like it's carrying the best bits of Mass Effect forward, and in an encouraging move, the developers have been collaborating with David Gaider.

Of course, David Gaider is best known as the lead writer on Dragon Age: Origins, Dragon Age 2 and Dragon Age: Inquisition - he's also often credited as the architect of its dark fantasy world Thedas. Gaider's post-BioWare career saw him open his own game development house Summerfall Studios, which most recently released an ambitious roleplaying musical called Stray Gods.

But he's now lending a hand to a game that's not too dissimilar to BioWare's other hugely famous roleplaying series, while still working on his own games at Summerfall.

"Alongside my work at Summerfall, I've also been collaborating with the Owlcat Games team on The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, focusing on certain aspects of the game's narrative. The Expanse has long been one of my favourite series, and so obviously I jumped at the opportunity to be involved," he wrote on BlueSky.

"The Owlcat team has been so great, it's really such a treat. One thing I enjoy is how responsive they are to the fans," Gaider added, pointing to how the studio recently recast the male version of its protagonist in response to feedback. The game's reworked and re-designed Martian Captain is now voiced by Blythe Melin.

The Expanse: Osiris Reborn shouldn't be confused for the other very Mass Effect-y RPG coming out next year, Exodus. Though it's good to hear that both upcoming projects have some BioWare veterans on board, especially after the famed developer was shut down and had its own promising, actual Mass Effect game cancelled.

Bertie enjoyed what he played of the upcoming game in Eurogamer's The Expanse preview, but also had some concerns about the developer's use of generative AI.

Slay the Spire 2's early access journey continues, and developer Mega Crit isn't skimping on what it's calling the roguelike deckbuilder's "biggest update yet." Update v0.113.0 goes into beta today, introducing a new character in The Fool. It also adds two new game modes, called Blitz and Dread.

If you want to opt into the beta branch and check out The Fool before the character is ready for the main game, just hop into the game's properties on Steam, go into the Game Versions & Betas tab, and select "public-beta" from the dropdown menu.

On top of the new character, there are two new game modes Blitz is "condensed and chaotic deckbuilding-focused mode" where the "Merchant's wares feel a bit off, the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters." A few months ago, Mega Crit said it was slowing down on updates so it could focus on "bigger, more impactful content," and it looks like we're starting to see the fruits of that pivot. Slay the Spire 2 launched back in March, and expect the game's early access period to be similar to the year-and-a-half it took the previous game to reach version 1.0, so it looks like we've got a fair few more updates to look forward to in the meantime.

We PC gamers are far from the belle of the AI ball.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Jensen Huang has resigned from his position as Nvidia CEO. That's such an odd sentence to write, as a huge part of my career as a tech journalist has revolved around covering Nvidia, its graphics cards, and its leather-jacketed chief.

As I write this article, I'm already seeing reactions on social media from PC gamers. Some are shocked, some are indifferent, and some appear to be celebrating. In terms of the latter, I'd imagine that's because the ex-Nvidia boss has become one of the most recognisable figures behind the great AI revolution, which, err, isn't popular within our hobby, to say the least.

Not only that, but RAM is ludicrously expensive, with storage not far behind. And graphics cards, Nvidia's gaming bread and butter? The price increases recently have been mind-boggling. All of these things are, in the main, AI server-demand induced, and Nvidia is behind the chips that power most of those servers, making vast amounts of money in the process.

And so on that level, I can understand why some might cheer his departure, equating the company's figurehead with Nvidia's new place in the AI economy as a whole—leaving us gamers in the lurch. But as far as I see it, Jensen Huang leaving the helm of Nvidia is unlikely to be a good thing for PC gaming.

I'll give you an unfortunate percentage: 7.4%. That's roughly how much of Nvidia's total revenue was brought in by gaming in the 2026 fiscal year. The company reported $193.7 billion in data center revenue. Its gaming division? $16 billion. That's despite the fact the company is estimated to hold 90% of the PC graphics card market share.

In terms of business fundamentals, Nvidia would be foolish to put more focus on gaming hardware while the AI cash cow continues to provide. Huang, however, still seemed reluctant to leave PC gaming entirely by the wayside during his tenure.

Those who have watched as many Nvidia GPU announcements as I have will know that walking on stage with a new graphics card, or gaming laptop, lit up Huang's face the most. 3D graphics was where the company began, after all, back when founders Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem sat down at a Denny's in San Jose and put together a business plan. Or so the story goes.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

But now, someone new will be steering the ship. Colette Kress, the company's executive vice president and chief financial officer will serve as interim CEO, while the search begins for Huang's permanent replacement.

Whoever they are, they'll be taking over an absolute titan of tech, the behemoth standing behind the US position in the great AI race, and a company that will need to convince its investors that the AI good times are far from over. How big a factor do you think consumer graphics cards are likely to be in those discussions?

Personally, I reckon they're going to be pretty far down the list of priorities. Because this is big business, money talks, and AI data centers are where most of the cash still lies. I wish that wasn't true, but the figures speak for themselves.

So, if Nvidia pivots even further away from gaming hardware, where might your next graphics card come from? There's always AMD, who's CEO has recently proudly declared it as "a data center-first company." Hmm, I'm not too confident on the focus there, either. Or Intel, which... oh jeez, you too?

I'm not saying consumer gaming hardware, or Nvidia graphics cards, are going to disappear entirely in the face of the AI onslaught. But what I am saying is that, love him or loathe him, Jensen Huang was still an advocate for PC gaming—at least out of sentimentality, if nothing else.

He who became one of the primary movers of the AI market now threatening our hobby, was also an integral part of PC gaming's success. But now, Nvidia is likely to be making some big changes, sans Huang—and I find it hard to believe that many of them will be in our favour.

You name it, if it's PC gaming hardware he'll write words about it, with opinions and everything.

#3828. Updated Xbox PC app promises 60% faster loading and easier access to games, but CEO Asha Sharma says there's "plenty more to do"

The Xbox PC app hasn't had the best track record in recent years, but Microsoft is promising that it's now much faster and easier to use than before.

Starting today, anyone part of the Xbox Insiders program can try out the new improvements. According to Microsoft, the updated Xbox PC app now boots up 60% faster, several pages can launch up to 50% faster, and in-app windows can open up to 65% faster. The company acknowledged that performance can vary based on your set up, internet connection, device, and so on.

The rest of the update involves "simpler navigation, updated filters, and new ways to organise your games," according to Xbox Wire, while social features are now included in the main navigation menu so you can start playing or chatting with friends quicker.

A faster Xbox PC app is certainly nice for players who regularly use it, though it's still missing a lot of the features that make Steam the go-to place to buy PC games. CEO Asha Sharma called the update "a meaningful improvement," but acknowledged there's still "plenty more to do."

Microsoft also said "it's easier to find what you're looking for" using the app's search function, and refreshed game cards and animations should give the platform "a cleaner look and feel."

Elsewhere, the revamped cloud gaming setup will roll out to even more people using web browsers, and more Xbox Insiders should hear about the program over the next few weeks. "The updated experience also makes it easier to find and play your games," the company said while bringing attention to its new light and dark modes. Supported smart TVs and VR headsets will get the updated cloud experience, as well.

90 Day: Florida is the latest entry in the 90 Day Fiancé franchise, and I have to ask if we've lost the plot. Sure, it seems and feels like the average TLC spinoff we'd expect to see on the 2026 TV schedule, minus the cornerstones of what makes this franchise what it is. Yes, beginning Monday, December 14th, those with TLC or an HBO Max subscription can see all the 90 Day couples living in Florida jam-packed into one show. This season teases a wedding between Cortney Reardanz and Phil, as well as a celebration for Jasmine Pineda. It sounds fun, but I'm still on the fence about it due to these two principles.

90 Day: Florida gives me pause for a couple of reasons, and they have to do with the foundation of the franchise. One detail is the fact that this entire spinoff takes place in one location. While we've seen this done before with 90 Day: The Last Resort or Hunt For Love, the resort was a matter of convenience rather than a series focused on individuals all living in one area. I mean, should a franchise that focuses on people finding love abroad have a spinoff based solely in one part of the United States?

It doesn't feel like we're going to get the best storylines with couples in the franchise, or that this is a handpicked selection of the best 90 Day has to offer. It's just all the cast members who live in Florida, which feels like this was just made out of convenience rather than actual fan interest.

90 Day: Florida feels like TLC attempting to make 90 Day Fiancé like the Real Housewives franchise. The problem is, what they're doing already exists, and in making a spinoff based solely on the fact that all these couples live in the same state, I question if it'll pull in the core audience that shows up for these shows.

I'm Shocked By How Much 90 Day Fiancé's Sarper Reportedly Made Doing Stand-Up Comedy

All this to say, it's not my money, so I'm curious to see how 90 Day: Florida will do and how audiences will respond. I do know there are rumors that Yara Dufren will be accused of cheating on Jovi, which is something I would love to know more about.

I also can't help but notice the timing of this spinoff lines up perfectly with Libby and Andrei Castravet announcing their exit from the franchise. They're also based in Florida, so is it possible they ended up leaving after not receiving an invite to appear? I'd love to know the details on that, especially in the aftermath of their feud with Alexei and Loren Brovarnik.

Whether I'm on board or not, though, I'll be watching 90 Day: Florida when it premieres, and I hope I'm wrong about this franchise not really feeling like it falls under the 90 Day Fiancé umbrella. I'll be eager to see what other viewers say as well, and if this ends up being a format that TLC sticks with for other states.

#3826. Xbox is testing a way to use your phone as a controller on smart TVs

Xbox is testing two new ways to play its cloud games, and one of them doesn't require a controller at all.

Announced on Xbox Wire on 4th November, the phone controller preview is rolling out on supported TVs wherever Xbox Cloud Gaming is available. The phone option - which works with both Android and iOS devices - lets you use your phone "as a controller when you don't have one nearby". Connect to your TV via QR code, and the controls open in your phone's browser.

The second preview, called cloud connect, is currently limited to the US and lets the new Xbox Nano controller talk to your cloud session over wi- fi instead of pairing directly with your TV to "help reduce input latency, so gameplay feels more responsive".

To try out the phone controls yourself, switch on Preview Features under Settings > Account in the latest version of the Xbox smart TV app.

Xbox has published a setup guide with full instructions, although you should note that both experiences "are still being tested", so the availability and supported games or devices "may be limited while [Xbox] learns from your feedback".

ICYMI, as of yesterday, anyone in the Xbox Insider Program can try Microsoft's updated Xbox PC app. The company claims it now boots up 60% faster, several pages can launch up to 50 percent faster, and in-app windows can open up to 65 percent faster.

#3825. Wardogs Season 3 brings an urban map, Limited Mode, and a 185,000-account ban wave

Wardogs' Season 3 will launch on 12th November, complete with a new urban map, a new Limited Mode, and a ban wave targeting 185,000 accounts.

Developer Bulkhead confirmed the details earlier this week, revealing plans for a full wipe and progression changes that it hopes will "recapture the shared discovery and sense of achievement that defined" the 100-player tactical shooter when it first launched in Early Access.

The new map will focus on close-quarters fighting, and for a "more level playing field", players can dip into Limited Mode, which offers "an alternative way to experience" the game as it restricts weapons, ammunition, armour, and vehicles.

While the full list of restrictions is still being decided, it currently includes FMJ-only ammunition, a Tier 2 armour cap, and a reduced attack vehicle selection.

"The mode is designed to preserve the feel of early-to-mid-game combat and reduce the advantage offered by more powerful equipment," the team said.

Bulkhead also confirmed seasons are getting longer. From now on, they’ll last three months, giving players "more time to work towards their goals before each wipe and the development team more time to prepare future updates". Progression will also be "brought closer to the pace of Season 1", following the studio’s acknowledgement that Season 2 accelerated "the journey too aggressively".

"Season 3 is about giving players a new battlefield to learn together and a progression journey worth spending time on," said Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer. "Longer seasons give everyone more room to reach their own goals, and give us the time to properly develop what comes next."

Alongside Season 3, Bulkhead revealed it has used machine learning to review is "activating further layers of its anti-cheat" after analysing 187 million hours of gameplay with help from machine learning. It says having close to four million unique players since launch gave it enough data to pull that work forward from next year.

"[E]xploiters, real-money traders, and gold-farming networks" have been permanently banned and lost their server-hosting privileges, and a player trust score is planned for 2027.

"Protecting the people who play Wardogs fairly is essential to everything we're building," Brammer added.

Bigger changes to the metagame, including a new progression system, are also due in 2027 as Bulkhead works towards Wardogs 1.0. Full Season 3 patch notes will be out before launch.

Wardogs launched in Steam Early Access on 10th September, and is due on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S in 2028.

Wardogs is one of the breakout successes of the year. In our early access Wardogs review, we said the game's mix of competitive shooters' best bits with something entirely of its own made it "a brilliantly refreshing take on the genre".

#3824. The end of DC as we know it: New DCU leadership will probably follow family-friendly Marvel formula, according to its new chief

It was fun while it lasted. The DCU, Warner Bros.’ response to the Marvel Cinematic Universe, is probably ending for good and switching from a darker, grittier approach to a family-friendly one that’s appealing to as many people as humanly possible. While this hasn’t exactly been confirmed by the DCU’s new leadership, previous comments from Jeremy Latcham strongly indicate this will be the future of DC on film.

In June of this year, Latcham, who came to take over DCU from James Gunn, said in an interview that he gave each of his Marvel projects the so-called “grandma test,” where he would ask whether his own grandma would find the movie appealing as someone who isn’t necessarily part of the core audience.

“And that became like a guiding light of, as we were developing the movies, I just had this sense of, ‘I don’t know if my grandma would like that,’ and that became the stand-in for, like, ‘Is this going to work for regular people that are outside of the bubble of Hollywood? What does this say for a regular family?” Latcham said (thanks, SlashFilm).

The new face of DC we are cooked. RIP Peacemaker and anything rated R pic.twitter.com/W50CYpfBeO

And this apparently extended as far as Marvel cutting out entire sections, jokes, or other parts of its movies because of a running joke at the studio saying Jeremy’s meemaw and peepaw wouldn’t like them. With that mindset, I think it is fairly safe to say R-rated, mature, dark, grim, and gritty DC movies we all know and love are out the window, because there is no way in hell a casual capes**t-brained moviegoer is going to be appealed to through stories like that of Peacemaker or Clayface.

This person brought untold billions to Marvel and Disney by following this exact formula in the early days of comic book movies, but we’re well beyond that point now. This is no longer an industry in its infancy needing to broaden its scope and vision to include as many people as possible and become commercially viable. The DCU movies, and especially its shows, have all been more or less successful. Yes, there are major flops like Supergirl, but let’s not pretend Gunn’s leadership didn’t turn the tide on an otherwise derelict ship aimlessly wandering the infinite waters of creative bankruptcy.

On the flip side, what Latcham’s approach inevitably led to is carbon-copy movies, each following the same structure and formula, remaining within a safe zone where the appeal to everyone results in the happiness of no one.

I will say this, though: while Latcham was at MCU, they did make a lot of good movies, like Iron Man and Iron Man 2 and the still-incredible Avengers: Age of Ultron (yeah, Ultron was right, fight me). But it is undeniable that his exact philosophy brought around the MCU’s bombastic failures, too.

And what’s worse, James Gunn himself has been liking comments saying Peacemaker is done for, and that, I think, is a real sign of the times.

Adam Driver and Miles Teller are the co-leads of a particularly thrilling entry on the 2026 movie schedule. The two actors – alongside the show-stopping Scarlett Johansson – headline Paper Tiger, the latest film from director James Gray. It tells the story of a family that gets wrapped up in shaky business dealings and, as a result, some characters keep secrets. CinemaBlend caught up with Teller and Driver and asked about their secret-keeping abilities, and it seems as far as their wives are concerned, they just can’t do it.

In the film, Teller and Driver play Irwin and Gary Pearl, respectively, who embark on a business venture (at Gary’s suggestion) involving the Gowanus Canal in 1980s New York. The two ultimately find themselves contending with the forces of the Russian mafia and, amid a portion of the conflict, Irwin’s wife, Hester (Johansson) is left in the dark. When CB caught up with the two leading men and asked if they would be able to keep big secrets from their significant other, and Driver dropped a funny take:

Would I have told her right away? Oh, yeah. Yeah, yeah, yeah…. My wife is kind of a [clairvoyant]. She can see into the future a little bit. No literally, but she can just tell….

Since 2013, Driver has been married to Joanne Tucker, with whom he shares two children. Based on his comments, it sounds like the Ferrari star knows better than to try to keep something from his wife. The sentiments drew laughs from Teller, but he also seemed to be able to empathize with the thoughts. Teller is married to Keleigh Sperry (who’s known for sharing fun videos online), and they’ve been married for over seven years. While discussing whether he’d keep a big secret from Sperry, Teller had this to say about his wife:

Yeah, Keleigh, can always sense when something’s… Even if I just eat something wrong, she's like, ‘Everything OK?’ I’m like, how did you…

It’s great to hear that the two stars strive to maintain transparency with their wives, though that also begs another question. Our Jeff McCobb went on to ask if the two would tell the truth only because they knew they couldn’t get away with a lie. However, they both clarified their thoughts on that front:

Considering their attitudes, I wonder if that tendency not to keep secrets also extends to the actors’ work. I mean, was Tucker aware that Driver was developing a Kylo Ren movie with Steven Soderbergh for a time, or is Sperry privy to any details regarding Teller’s involvement in Top Gun 3? I’d also like to know if the pair’s co-star, Johansson, also kept secrets from hubby Colin Jost while she was “wrapped up” in Marvel movies. I could just be overthinking this, and maybe the stars’ spouses don’t even care to know such information. Regardless, it’s still interesting to consider.

What isn’t a secret, though, is that Paper Tiger is proving to be an extremely buzzy title, and James Gray and co. are receiving considerable praise from critics. The Armageddon Time director seems to have delivered yet another classic, and it may even yield some recognition this awards season. For now, though, anyone who wants to see Adam Driver and Miles Teller keep secrets (on screen and not in real life) can check out their new movie, which opens in limited release on November 13 and opens nationwide on November 20.

#3822. GTA 6 shoots to the moon and past Cyberpunk’s 2020 hype train to become most-preordered game of all time

GTA 6 is looking to become the biggest game of all time, and its pre-orders alone almost give it that title.

It was bound to happen anyway, but we’re happy to report GTA 6 has officially surpassed Cyberpunk 2077‘s pre-order record with over 10.3 million copies sold ahead of Nov. 19. This figure steadily continues to rise as most pre-orders happen within a week or even days of a game’s launch, so we expect it to bloat even more by this time next week.

This is according to Sensor Tower, which has a dedicated GTA 6 sales tracking tool currently reporting 10.31 million copies sold as pre-orders. In total, the game has earned over a billion USD before it even came out, and that is from the pre-orders alone, not including the horrible collector’s edition or officially licensed merch. Of this billion, 750m came from the PlayStation Store, but surprisingly, 250m were generated via Xbox. Most people seem to be purchasing the $100 edition, with 7.73 million units sold on the PS Store, and 2.58m on Xbox.

What this tells me is people are more than comfortable spending extra bucks on what they perceive as a “good deal,” which could carry incredible implications for the future of gaming, especially in the AAA sphere. If people wanna spend $100 on this, they probably would want to dish out that much money on other games, too, and I don’t think it’ll be long before the standard AAA price is adjusted from the $70-80 range to $90-100. This is going to have a horrible impact on those not using USD as their currency, with the Euro always getting a 10-15 percent worse deal, and regional pricing oftentimes making games nigh-unpurchasable in some parts of the world.

At any rate, though, these pre-order numbers signal that GTA 6 is about to have a killer first week on the market, with previous projections looking at around $5 billion by the end of its opening weekend, if not more. It is by all means going to be the biggest game ever made, even if it doesn’t turn out to be the best, and when its Online version drops, I reckon Rockstar will be noting down double-digit billions of income every quarter from this one title alone.

25 OG Xbox titles are now on PC, and it's an utterly bizarre list of games

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

This weekend marks Xbox's 25th birthday, and while any celebration of the milestone is going to be muted in view of the layoff bloodbath Microsoft is currently engaging in, the gaming division is taking steps to keep us thinking about the brand in a positive light. That includes a fresh expansion to the list of original Xbox games that are now backwards compatible on PC.

After the four original Xbox games that Microsoft brought to PC earlier this year, another 21 have joined the list – a total of 25 games for the console's 25th birthday. The new list of games is an utterly bizarre one, largely dominated by LucasArts titles. That includes plenty of beloved Star Wars titles, alongside largely forgotten obscurities like Secret Weapons Over Normandy and Thrillville.

Some of the titles you might recognize, like Star Wars classics Battlefront 2, Jedi Outcast, and Knights of the Old Republic, are odd choices in themselves, since those games are already available on PC. Assuming Xbox is using the same emulation-based solution to port these games, they're all going to be substantially worse experiences than simply picking up the native PC versions for the same price on Steam.

That goes double for The Elder Scrolls 3: Morrowind, which is also on the list of newly added games. The Xbox version of Morrowind was a stunning technical achievement back in 2002, but it was notoriously janky even at the time, filled with bugs and technical limitations that have been robustly addressed on PC. I struggle to come up with a compelling reason anyone would want to play this version over the PC original today, especially with all the mods available for the RPG.

There are two games I absolutely will not complain about, however: TimeSplitters 2 and TimeSplitters: Future Perfect. Developed by the Rare veterans at Free Radical Design, the TimeSplitters series was a spiritual successor to classic N64 games GoldenEye and Perfect Dark, refreshing the FPS gameplay for a new generation with fun weapon gimmicks and charmingly goofy characters.

TimeSplitters never moved beyond cult classic status, and attempts to revive the series ended in failure. None of these games ever got PC ports, which makes their inclusion arguably the most notable part of this Xbox backwards compatibility update.

#3820. Assassin's Creed is reportedly going to ancient Rome, while a mobile spin-off heads to Jerusalem

Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games, and one of them is set in ancient Rome.

That's according to YouTuber Xj0nathan, who says the Rome game is codenamed Mars. He claims two sources with access to Ubisoft's backend systems backed up the information, and that the setting will likely be linked to the upcoming Assassin's Creed TV series.

If Mars does move into full production, don't hold your breath - Insider Gaming doesn't expect us to hear anything about it until 2029 or 2030.

Assassin's Creed has visited Rome before, in 2010’s Brotherhood, but that was the Renaissance version of the city.

The leak comes less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

Sony has delayed its Pulse Elevate wireless speakers indefinitely, less than a week before they were due to launch.

The news came in a 6th November update to Sony’s original announcement on the PlayStation Blog, first spotted by IGN. Quality testing has turned up a "production issue", Sony said, and there's no new release date yet.

"As part of our ongoing quality testing of Pulse Elevate speakers, we have identified a production issue with the product and have made the decision to delay the launch," the statement reads. "The additional time will allow us to ensure the product will deliver the experience we intended for our players. We apologise for the delay and appreciate your patience and understanding. We look forward to bringing Pulse Elevate to players soon."

The speakers were set to go on sale worldwide on 12th November, and pre-orders opened in September. It's unclear what, exactly, happens to those orders, but we'll update as and when we find out more.

Sony revealed Pulse Elevate in September 2025 as its first wireless speakers for desktop gaming. They sit alongside the Pulse Elite headset and Pulse Explore earbuds, and cost £199.99 ($219.99).

They connect to PS5, PC, Mac, and PlayStation Portal via PlayStation Link, and can pair with a phone over Bluetooth at the same time. There's also a microphone in the right speaker with what Sony calls "AI-enhanced noise rejection".

Midnight Black was due to be available everywhere, while the White version was limited to a handful of countries, including the UK.

Alongside the Pulse Elevate speakers, Sony revealed a range of hardware in September 2025, including a 27-inch gaming monitor that's coming only to the US and Japan.

Drew Barrymore is all in when it comes to lining up guests for her talk show.

Drew Barrymore is undeniably charming, and her feel-good talk show is like the living embodiment of a warm hug. She admits to being big on joy, laughter, and feeling good, and she clearly carries that over into everything she does, including The Drew Barrymore Show, currently on the 2026 TV schedule. If you want a daily dose of optimism and sincerity, she’s the actress and host you can count on to bring it.

I say all of this because it makes it easy to understand why the 50 First Dates star goes above and beyond to pursue the guests she wants on the Emmy-winning show. At a time when Kelly Clarkson has wrapped up her own talk show after its seventh season, Barrymore seems to be thriving and still very involved with a Season 7 of her own. A source explained to Globe that part of the secret to her success is that she’s not afraid to take matters into her own hands. The source was quoted as saying:

Drew isn’t afraid to pick up the phone and personally ask agents to book their clients on the show. She does it all the time – and it works!

Drew Barrymore got her start as a child actor in movies like E.T. and Firestarter before finding success as an adult in the ‘90s with Scream, The Wedding Singer, Ever After and Never Been Kissed. She’s also been very honest about her own personal and family strife, even discussing her current perimenopause journey, having been in the public eye for so long, which also helps to make her chat show feel like a safe space for the conversations she has with her guests.

Where celebrities used to talk to Barbara Walters knowing that she would likely make them cry with her questions, the guests on The Drew Barrymore Show know that if they end up crying with her, she’ll be there to also give them a hug. It’s nice to know that, if she’s going to make that extra effort to pick up the phone and personally ask agents to book their clients on the show, she also backs it up with her actions. The Globe’s source went on to say:

But there’s also been some re-evaluating of the whole series now that it’s got five years under its belt and Kelly Clarkson seems to be pulling back from her own daytime show.

Barrymore has created such an intimate vibe with her guests that personal boundaries have essentially been thrown out the window. It will be interesting to see how and if the series will evolve, especially now that Kelly Clarkson is moving on to other ventures of her own.

After so many seasons under her belt now, it would actually be a great time for Barrymore to shake things up a bit while maintaining the wild energy that is unconventional but still very Drew. I don’t know what that could translate to, so I’ll leave that to the Santa Clarita Diet star who’s clearly doing something right with the continued success of her talk show. But I will be tuning in to see the connection she has with her guests, as that will no doubt continue.

The Drew Barrymore Show is in daytime syndication, having already been renewed for Season 8, extending its run through 2028. It can also be watched with an active Paramount+ subscription.

Tae Kim, author of The Nvidia Way, thinks there are some promising alternatives to Huang.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There is also one excellent external candidate who has been very successful outside of Nvidia and offers both technical expertise and solid business management experience. Employees loved working for him. Either one would be great.November 11, 2026

We thought it might be coming, and it's here: Jensen Huang is no longer CEO of Nvidia, as he has resigned following an admitted affair, and an additional alleged one.

It wasn't unexpected, and both before and after the announcement there has been a lot of talk about how it would be a bad decision and could spell very bad news for Nvidia. And, well, there's certainly some truth in that given we saw company share prices drop after reports of Huang's alleged second affair came to light.

After perusing X for a while today, the general sentiment seems to be that Huang was so incredibly central to Nvidia that the company couldn't possibly do well without him. Or at the very least, nowhere near as well as it would with Jensen sticking at the helm. Ditto the AI market in general.

But not everyone agrees. In fact, one of the most credible voices on Nvidia reckons there are "strong" and "excellent" candidates for a replacement. Tae Kim wrote the most well-known, authoritative book on the company—The Nvidia Way—and yesterday they explained:

"Many people have cited my book as saying Nvidia would be completely lost without Jensen Huang. My views have evolved in the several years since I wrote those passages. I now believe there is a strong internal candidate with the technical expertise, experience, customer relationships and respect of employees needed to lead Nvidia effectively into its next chapter."

"There is also one excellent external candidate who has been very successful outside of Nvidia and offers both technical expertise and solid business management experience. Employees loved working for him. Either one would be great."

They're certainly optimistic comments, but your guess is as good as mine as to who they might be referring to—presumably someone on the list of potential replacement CEO candidates I put together earlier.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

We now know that the actual interim CEO is Colette Kress—exactly who we predicted it would be. I'm not sure whether that's who Kim had in mind, given they decided, for some strange reason, to not mention who they were thinking of by name. But if not, there's still room for the next proper CEO to be one of those he has in mind.

This being said, Jensen Huang's status, drive, and deep familiarity with the company and the market are undoubtedly unparalleled. I think you'd find it difficult to pin down anyone who could reasonably disagree with that. In which case, while Nvidia might not be "completely lost", it's hard to say it will be as oriented as it would be with Huang still at the helm.

#3814. Star Wars Zero Company studio Bit Reactor lays off staff, a month after bringing furloughed developers back

"While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together."

Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff, a month after bringing some of its furloughed team back to work.

Several developers announced on LinkedIn on Friday, 6th November, that they had been let go, as first reported by Bespin Bulletin. Bit Reactor hasn't said how many people are affected.

Among them is senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who spent three and a half years working on Zero Company, from pre-production to launch, and was laid off after a three-month furlough. UI engineer Tyler Eichten, who worked on much of the on-screen UI for the game's tactical missions, and Ryan Mosher from the QA team have also confirmed they were let go.

"While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote. "It was a privilege to ship a game with you."

Bit Reactor furloughed most of its staff in the weeks before Zero Company launched on 27th August, with one source putting the figure at roughly 80 percent. The studio appeared to have run out of money just short of release.

The game did well regardless, and is thought to have sold more than a million copies within a month. Then, in a message shared on Bluesky on 7th October, CEO Greg Foertsch said the studio had "started the process of returning more of our team back to work". Asking staff to step away so close to launch was "an incredibly difficult decision", he said, "but one that was necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as possible".

It's thought more than half the studio returned, though not everyone went back on full pay. It's not clear whether any of those who returned were among the people laid off this week.

In Eurogamer's Star Wars Zero Company review, we awarded the game four out of five stars, saying, "an already winning genre is matched with the perfect setting in this earnest, heartfelt, smart and slightly ramshackle turn-based tactics gem".

#3813. The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past’s Polish Geralt VA will be tuned with AI due to the actor’s health concerns

The actor's health severely impacted the sound of his voice.

AI is a moral conundrum in itself. It’s hard to justify its usage, and the only times people do find reasons for its application, they cite “productivity” as the end-all be-all of our modern, ever-corporatized world. But there could be proper and respectful and meaningful ways to use artificial intelligence, though all that could also be a very slippery slope.

As Game File reports, The Witcher 3‘s Polish Geralt of Rivia actor, Jacek Rozenek, was set to reprise his role for Songs of the Past, TW3‘s upcoming expansion pack. However, Rozenek had suffered a stroke in 2019, losing his speech altogether for several months. As of 2021, Rozenek recovered somewhat and managed to record a few extra lines for The Witcher 3‘s next-gen update, but even that brief work left him utterly exhausted.

The studio was more than eager to bring him back for Songs of the Past, but they soon discovered his voice was much rougher and lower than before, and since this new expansion would require a ton of entirely new and fairly violent voice lines for combat and other scenes, CDPR got in touch with a Ukrainian AI company, Respeecher, all with the actor’s own blessing.

Respeecher had already helped CDPR emulate the Polish voice for Cyberpunk’s Viktor as his actor, Miłogost Reczek, had died in 2021. However, this case will be altogether different, as Rozenek would still be doing the lines, but with Respeecher applied to tune his voice to make it more similar to how he sounded before.

Game File’s Stephen Totilo believes the difference is quite significant and that this altered voice sounds much closer to Rozenek’s original performance. However, even CDPR is aware of the ethical implications of using AI, especially in voice acting, but it does believe this is one of those instances where applying it is quite acceptable.

I don’t know if I agree with that statement necessarily. I mean, Rozenek is still doing the lines himself, so why not allow for change? It’s been 12 years since the original game’s performances were captured, and it’s not like we can stop people from aging, especially when such extraordinary things as Rozenek’s health issues happen.

I was at Gamescom this year and saw Songs of the Past in English. Doug Cockle, who also suffered from cancer for a while between Blood and Wine and SotP, also had his voice altered quite a bit. He sounds a lot rougher than before, and in some instances his voice range is actually higher than he might have been aiming for. It’s different, to say the least, but I don’t see why AI would be used to make him sound like he were 12 years younger. He isn’t. The world isn’t.

I guess this was at least done with the acquiescence and blessing of the actor himself, so in some sense it is as ethical as can be, but I don’t think it’s a really good idea to set a precedent that voice actors cannot mature and change and allow their voices to alter because they wouldn’t sound right anymore, and especially so in circumstances where you just decide to make another expansion for a 12-year-old game.

Playground Games is ramping up its marketing efforts for its upcoming Fable revival, and a new gameplay showcase seems to confirm the return of enemy Nymphs, which we haven't seen since the original Fable back in 2004.

The new Official Quest Gameplay trailer, released as part of Xbox's 25th anniversary shenanigans, shows a darker side to Albion than we're used to seeing, and I mean that literally. After cranking up the brightness on my monitor, I could see that the footage shows a female hero character seeking out her village's mysterious assailant with the help of a character named Arden. Tracing the attacker's path leads the duo through a heavily wooded forest with giant thorny vines and eventually, a confrontation with some familiar-looking foes outside a cave entrance.

Again, everything is dark in this trailer, but from what I can tell these fellas look a whole lot like the Wood Nymphs, which are one of two species of fairy-like creatures, the other being Water Nymphs, from OG Fable back in the day. They're referred to as "cursed monsters" in the quest log, but c'mon, those are fairies. They're little magical winged humanoids with big heads and tree bark-like skin, and they flutter around in clouds of colorful orbs and shoot ethereal projectiles your way. If that isn't a Wood Nymph, well then I don't know what a Wood Nymph is. And believe me, I know a thing or two about Wood Nymphs.

Anyway, otherwise the trailer is fairly unremarkable. Not in a bad way, just in a way that doesn't reveal anything super new or exciting to talk about, which makes sense considering we're just a few short months away from getting to play the game. Fable is out on PS5, Xbox Series X, and PC on February 23.

News broke a few days ago that Universal Orlando’s beloved mascot Earl the Squirrel would be hitting a big milestone this year. He’s headed to the 100th Annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, and if you plan to watch on NBC or with your Peacock subscription, you’ll be able to see him getting his own giant balloon. It’s a big anniversary for the Thanksgiving parade, but it’s also a solid one for Earl, who turns 5 this year. Let’s talk out what we know.

Here at CinemaBlend, we’ve been big fans of Earl The Squirrel for a while. The story behind Earl goes that Earl the Squirrel was a real mammal who burrowed in Universal Studios’ giant Christmas tree in Orlando in the early aughts. One of the best parts of being at Universal Studios around the holidays is the lighting of the Christmas tree, and the original Earl liked to chew on the aforementioned lights.

Someone on the team jokingly put a stuffed squirrel in the Christmas tree in homage, and then in 2021, someone had the bright idea to bring Earl into the parks officially.

Now, he’s the mascot, and most definitely one of the cool Easter egg found throughout the parks. I visited during the holidays last year and saw him cutely burrowing in the big Christmas tree. I’ve also caught Earl in the Tribute store in the past, and a life-size version of Earl does meet-and-greets throughout the holiday season. Finding him on the tree is still a sort of yearly scavenger hunt.

However, I get the sneaking suspicion anyone watching the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade won’t have any trouble spotting Earl. That’s because he’s going to be 30.4 feet tall and 14.5 feet wide. Literally, you won’t be able to miss him.

I haven’t been to the real-life Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York, but Universal Orlando already offers the next best thing: The Holiday Parade Featuring Macys. The theme park actually has had ties to the Macy’s Parade for years, and even if you aren’t normally a parade person, bringing the giant balloons into the theme park is real feat, and impressive to see. A visit around the holiday season is worth it for the parade alone.

The holiday season kicks off this weekend at Universal Orlando, starting on Saturday, November 14th, and Earle will join The Holiday Parade lineup in early December. For now, you can catch The Grinch in action, or check out the Red Coconut Club's alpine makeover. This year, Universal is also once again upping its food game, and you can try out one of the many new cabin-style holiday food kiosks featuring items like Christmas Tree waffles, red-nose reindeer donuts, oh and Earl gets a shoutout there too with Earl The Squirrel’s hazelnut dot cake.

I’m not even getting into the hot chocolate options, which are usually my personal favorite snack this time of year. (Well, as long as it’s not 90 degrees out.)

All in all, there’s a lot to look forward to if you’re planning a trip to the parks, and there are special tickets being offered this holiday season. You can find out more on the Universal Orlando site.

Jessica Rawden is Managing Editor at CinemaBlend. She’s been kicking out news stories since 2007 and joined the full-time staff in 2014. #3809. Skyrim celebrates its 15th birthday, and I hope Bethesda has learned something in all that time

The games it made since don't inspire much hope, though.

On the eleventh day of the eleventh month of the eleventh year of the 21st century, the world was graced by The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim. Bethesda’s crowning achievement, Skyrim remains one of the most influential games of all time, and I think we can safely say it’s most likely the biggest RPG ever made.

I was 10 when Skyrim first dropped, but even I remember how the online landscape was reshaped around it as soon as it came out. It was a nuclear hit, one that Bethesda will not be able to match 15 years down the line. It expanded on Bethesda’s growing ambition to make a massive game, a sandbox where you are free to do as you wish, to build as you want, to join whomever. It was liberating, a breath of cool northern air sweeping over the world of gaming and cementing one word in eternity: dragonborn.

Everyone knows just about every major plot beat from Skyrim, and untold billions of views have accumulated on YouTube and other social media platforms through videos dedicated to its lore, gameplay, and, most importantly, memes. Skyrim suffered, and still does, from the same janky bugs and issues all Bethesda games share, but that somehow made it more charming. The whole package is just good, but it did make a bunch of mistakes and fall short in many areas I wish Bethesda would never repeat.

But it did. It did in Fallout 4, and again in Starfield. But perhaps The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel will break the cycle.

Which cycle, I hear you ask? The cycle of dumbing every system down from game to game, focusing on turning RPGs into glorified first-person shooters (remember the Skyrim with guns joke?) and robbing the world of Tamriel of meaningful stories, characters, narratives and, crucially, choices on behalf of the player that are actual choices that make significant changes to the world state and alter the course of history itself. Skyrim was the beginning of the end for Bethesda’s RPG-ness. Both it and the games that followed took liberty to an extreme, never locking the player into any role to play. There were some exclusive decisions, such as the Stormcloaks vs. the Imperials ordeal, but that’s about it.

The game simply allowed you to do too much, and that stripped both the gameplay down to its barest and reduced the world to a bunch of coexisting groups who, despite nominal conflicts, do not in truth stand in opposition to each other. You shouldn’t be able to join every faction, play every class, do everything under the sun in one playthrough. This is not GTA. It’s an RPG. Give us roles to play. See what Baldur’s Gate 3 has done.

Fifteen years, a decade and a half, and Bethesda is still unwilling to part with its do-everything, be-anything approach, and I hope to God TES6 changes that. It’s not probable, but I pray it’s possible.

The happiest time of year is just around the corner, folks. The PC Gaming Show: Most Wanted sponsored by Pot Noodle will be airing December 3rd, and we'll be counting down The Council's 20 most anticipated games.

There's one major change this year, though. We've gone from counting down the top 25 games to the top 20. We've made this decision to ensure each game gets its time in the spotlight, meaning the show will be more enjoyable to watch. Also, The Council have recently unionised and refuse to count more until we agree to give them bathroom breaks, which we simply will not do.

The Council remains, as ever, an inscrutable bunch of journalists, developers, celebrities, creators, streamers, gaming luminaries, and just generally people whose opinion on videogames carries some weight.

Each year, we knock our heads together and puzzle over how to whittle down the thousands of upcoming games into a list of just 100. Several factors go into this, such as how many wishlists a game has on Steam, how interesting a trailer is, the position of the stars at the time a game was first announced, and generally just how excited those of us at PC Gamer are for a title.

The full list awaits below, and the top 20 are nestled within it, but you'll never be able to figure out which ones they are. And if you do, please don't share your findings on the internet or you'll ruin the whole show. You'll notice there are fewer than 100 games, and that's because each year, some come out before the show or unfortunately get cancelled. Try as we might, we can't get The Council to predict the future—we'd all be retired by now if they could.

The Council gives each game they're excited for a score from one to five, with one being passingly curious to five being intensely, worryingly hyped. If a member has no interest in a game at all, they simply don't vote on it and that is counted as a zero.

We also take into account how many members of The Council voted for each game so that any with the same average score have a reliable tiebreaker. Some other factors go into the weighting, too, like if we've had no news about a game in a long time or, again, where the stars are and what they think of the whole thing.

#3807. Missing teenager rescued after reaching out to another player in Among Us

"Our priority in this case was the safe return of the minor victim."

A teenager who went missing in Utah more than 17 months ago has been rescued from a home in Oregon after she got in touch with another young player in Among Us.

According to a federal criminal complaint reported by Newsweek and KUTV (via IGN), the girl, who was 15 when she disappeared from Garden City, Utah, on 29th May 2025, began chatting with another teenager in Among Us on or around 15th October this year.

The pair later moved their conversation to a different social media app, where she told them who she was and that she was being held against her will in Oregon. She had been given a phone with no cellular data, which meant she could only get online via wi-fi.

The other teen told their parent, who contacted the FBI on 1st November. Agents listened in on a video call between the parent and the girl, and she was recovered from the house later that day. She is now 17.

Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, of Huntington, Oregon, was arrested during a traffic stop.

According to the US Attorney's Office for the District of Utah, he allegedly met the girl online in May 2025, then drove to Utah to pick her up and took her back to his home across state lines. He was charged on 2nd November with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity, and made his first court appearance in Boise, Idaho, on 4th November.

"Our priority in this case was the safe return of the minor victim," said US Attorney Melissa Holyoak. "Those who allegedly exploit and prey upon the most vulnerable members of our communities will be relentlessly investigated and held accountable."

Utah's US Attorney's Office stresses that a complaint is merely an allegation, and that all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.

#3806. Saving Mass Effect would take $200m+, says BioWare co-founder

Anyone hoping to buy Mass Effect from EA and finish what BioWare started needs to get saving now, as it could cost over $200 million (£150m).

That's according to BioWare co-founder Trent Oster, who reckons that's what a new Mass Effect game would need to meet fans' expectations.

"The scary component of Mass Effect is the audience is going to want the best of 'AAA' development," Oster said on Twitter/X, as spotted by GamesRadar.

The scary component of Mass Effect is the audience is going to want the best of “AAA” development. Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200M+. That is a big number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work.

"Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200M+. That is a big number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work."

He did add that it could be done for less, though. "That said, I think it can be done well for less than that amount with a disciplined approach and an experienced team," Oster said.

"I think a game could be done cheaper, if you kept it simple and hit the big beats," he added in a separate tweet. "It wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept. The big push would be getting the IP free. The fans deserve more than one game."

I think a game could be done cheaper, if you kept it simple and hit the big beats. It wouldn’t be what the team described in the Universe concept. The big push would be getting the IP free. The fans deserve more than one game.

Oster's comments come as the #SaveMassEffect campaign continues to grow following EA's decision to close BioWare and cancel Mass Effect 5. Fans want EA to keep making Mass Effect games, or hand the series over to a studio that will.

Oster has backed the campaign too. "I love seeing all the energy around #SaveMassEffect," he wrote on 4th November. "I think there is a still a great thesis for a well-funded RPG developer who can deliver. Makes me want to get some of the original band back together."

EA has not confirmed whether or not it would consider selling the IP.

The petition created to save BioWare's well-loved sci-fi RPG, Mass Effect, topped 185,000 signatures in just days. It's now exceeded 317,000. Joe Smith, credited with starting the petition, isn't necessarily asking EA to change its mind about BioWare; instead, the petition calls for "decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect".

We said a sad farewell to BioWare last month. The closure, which came just months after Saudi Arabia's $55bn leveraged buyout of EA, was anticipated by experts, but drew widespread condemnation and messages of sympathy from across the industry.

A new report claims EA closed BioWare because it was forced to choose between investing in one of two sci-fi projects: a new Mass Effect game or a new Star Wars Battlefront game. And it chose the latter.

Fans are trying other routes to keep BioWare's doors open, too. Canadian fans of the studio have escalated their grievances to the governmental level, calling on the Canadian Government to step in and save the studio from closure, seemingly after Canada's New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis called on the government to do so.

#3805. All weapon evolutions in Warhammer Survivors

Warhammer Survivors has several weapon evolutions to unlock, and you can use them to power up your equipment. These require you to combine the weapons with specific items to unlock their passives.

The following table has a list of 21 different weapon evolutions.

While the Age of Sigmar evolutions share the Nuln Oil and D6 Dice with the 40K universe, the rest of them are unique.

#3802. Phasmophobia players raise over $230,000 for heart charity, more than double last year's total

The Phasmophobia community has raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.

Developer Kinetic Games announced the final figure for this year's Ghost Hunts for Hearts event on 6th November. The charity drive ran from 26th October to 2nd November, and more than 500 streamers signed up to take part. That's the biggest turnout yet for a creator fundraiser run by Heart Liive, the American Heart Association's streaming initiative.

Last year's event raised a little over $100,000.

Congratulations, Ghost Hunters, you've surpassed the community target and raised over $200,000 for our friends at @Heart_Liive!Your kindness and generosity will not go unrewarded, log in to Phasmophobia before the 15th November to claim the Animated AHA Advocate ID Card &… pic.twitter.com/KFQKaqXNCl

Streamers who fundraised could hand out an event-exclusive Advocate ID Card and Badge to their viewers as a Twitch Drop. Kinetic set a target of $200,000 at the start of the week, and once players sailed past it, an animated version of the card and badge set unlocked for all.

"The Phasmophobia community never fails to amaze us, and this year they've outdone themselves," said Tom Dent, lead social media and player experience manager at Kinetic Games. "Thank you to every streamer, viewer and player who took part."

Phasmophobia launched in Early Access in September 2020, and sends teams of up to four players into haunted locations to gather evidence of what's lurking there.

The studio also launched a publishing arm, Kinetic Publishing, earlier this year. Its first game, the starship job simulator Contact Protocol, is due out in spring 2027.

Phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2, although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this year, Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027, as the studio said it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Update. The studio ended up apologising to players for issues with the long-awaited update, admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".

Warning! The following contains spoilers for the NCIS episode "Speechless." Stream the episode with a Paramount+ subscription, and read at your own risk!

The latest episode of NCIS was a special one for Katrina Law, as the Jessica Knight actress co-starred in it with her daughter. Law told CinemaBlend her kid knocked it out of the park, but she was ready from the moment it was suggested to shut it down if she wasn't ready.

I had a chance to speak to the actress ahead of the episode's airing on the 2026 TV schedule. Law explained that her daughter, Kinley Andreen, actually pitched the idea of coming on the show, so when an opportunity came up, she was asked about having her on. While she was thrilled to give her daughter a chance to be on the series, the actress explained she wanted her kid to earn it through an audition:

There was a part of me going, like, if she's not really good, I'm not going to make [them cast her], I'm not going to, like, put everybody through this experience. She nailed that audition within 20 minutes.

Things went well, and Andreen booked her debut acting appearance as Chloe in NCIS. I was, frankly, a bit surprised to learn it was her first time acting, because I would've assumed she'd been doing it a while based on her performance. However, she'd never done traditional acting outside of school play performances. Did we all just witness the beginning of a future A-lister's career in television?

Due to that lack of experience, Katrina Law said she wanted to have her daughter go through the audition process to see if she's up for the challenge, but told us she couldn't be prouder of how she did:

It was a four-page audition...she picked up all the beats, she had props, she was doing different notes, there was an emotional arc, she memorized all the lines, was completely off book, and I'm like, there are adults who have to spend two days doing this just to prep for this moment, and you got it in 20 minutes. It was amazing.

Law and her daughter also got to display their fluency in Mandarin after the agents were shocked to find the little girl they found was bilingual. It was quite an acting debut, which makes me all the more thankful she pulled it off.

Jessica Knight's run in Season 24 of NCIS is off to a slow start, but the seeds are being planted for her to have a larger role later this season. Her constant monitoring of Tony DiNozzo for Ziva screams that a future team-up is in the works, which I'm very excited to see.

As for what's next for her daughter, who knows where we'll see Kinley Andreen show up next? There's nothing wrong with being a nepo baby when it comes to Hollywood, especially if you have the talent to back it up. Maybe if NCIS can stay on the air another 20+ years, we'll see Andreen come back and play an agent on the series!

For now, I'm just content we have a solid block of NCIS to enjoy on Tuesday nights. Tune in to CBS on those nights for a healthy dose of nostalgia, as the lineup is loaded with classic NCIS actors.

#3799. Ocarina of Time remake datamine suggests Master Quest is on the way

Ocarina of Time's notoriously tricky Master Quest mode could be making a comeback in the new remake.

Dataminer MrCheeze shared a list of strings from the remake's files on Bluesky, several of which tie the tag "MQ" to dungeons like Dodongo's Cavern.

In a follow-up, as spotted by TheGamer, they pointed to further entries, including "HasMQ", "IsMQModeExist", "NewGameMQ", and "ReleaseMQ".

Fellow dataminer OatmealDome added on Twitter/X that the mode will be unlocked by owning DLC, rather than arriving in an update, though "the data is incomplete". "I can confirm that the world is mirrored and dungeons are modified (e.g. cows in Jabu-Jabu's Belly)," they said.

If you've not played it, Master Quest is a remixed version of Ocarina of Time with rearranged dungeons and tougher puzzles. It first appeared as a bonus disc on GameCube, then came back in 2011's Ocarina of Time 3D, which unlocked it after you finished the main game. That version also mirrored the whole world, which matches what OatmealDome has found, and had enemies deal double damage.

[Ocarina of Time] #ootspoilersThere is data in the game files for Master Quest. It will be unlocked by *owning DLC* - it is not just an update.The data is incomplete, but I can confirm that the world is mirrored and dungeons are modified (e.g. cows in Jabu-Jabu's Belly).

As with any datamine, there's no guarantee it'll ever see the light of day. Nintendo hasn't announced any DLC for the remake, and it's not clear whether Master Quest would be free, like it was on 3DS, or paid.

The Ocarina of Time remake launched on Switch 2 on 5th November. Donlan called the new version an "astonishing remake" in his five-star Eurogamer Ocarina of Time review.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Kevin Feige says Doctor Doom isn't a variant of Tony Stark... despite that confusing Avengers: Endgame Encore post-credits scene making us think otherwise.

"People wondered, ‘Is Doom just a variant of another character? Is this just a shortcut to bringing back another character?’ The answer is no. He’s Victor Von Doom," Feige told Empire.

In one of several post-credits scenes that were added to the re-release of Avengers: Doomsday, Tony Stark is seen forging what appears to be a Doctor Doom mask. How are we not supposed to think that this implies Tony and Victor Von Doom are one and the same (aside from being played by the same actor)?

Even Variety posed a theory a little while ago that Doctor Doom is a variant of Iron Man from another planet, but it must be said again that Victor Von Doom and Tony Stark are completely separate characters in the comics. They go head-to-head in the 2008 comic book Iron Man: Legacy of Doom (which Downey was seen reading as part of his Doomsday prep). I hear you, though: How is the movie going to explain away Tony Stark and Doom having the same face? Well, he's rarely ever unmasked in the comics... so I just kind of figured the Russos were going to rely heavily on that. We'll see come December.

Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters in the UK on December 16 and in the US on December 18. For more, check out our guides to the Marvel timeline and how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

#3796. COD: Modern Warfare 4 gets a surprisingly sudden free trial, so you can see what the game's extraction mode DMZ is like

Activision has released the first trial for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's extraction mode DMZ. The trial is available across PC (Steam / Battlenet), PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S until Wednesday, 11th November.

The free trial only includes access to DMZ and no other part of Modern Warfare 4, such as multiplayer or the campaign. And while it's not uncommon for Call of Duty titles to make some of their modes available for free for a limited time, the timing of this DMZ taster is notable.

DMZ launched days before Modern Warfare 4's 23rd October release date, meaning this first trial has arrived just two weeks after the game's full launch. By comparison, Black Ops 7's Endgame mode had its first free trial months after launch, in the game's third season. That said, Endgame continued to be freely available until Season 6.

The DMZ trial also coincides with the launch of Modern Warfare 4's iteration of free-to-play Call of Duty battle royale mode Warzone, and Season 1. Indeed, both DMZ and the new Warzone take place on the same Hajin map, so even if you don't decide to buy the full game to continue playing DMZ, some of that map knowledge will certainly transfer to Warzone.

The DMZ trial does not appear to have any limits, meaning you can climb the ranks, access Story Missions - the only way to play PvE, with caveats - and complete Orders to your heart's content. That includes X01, the new endgame dungeon-like area available to experienced and fully-equipped players.

DMZ players who've been asking Infinity Ward to offer a PvE-only playlist of the PvPvE mode will certainly be happy with the influx of new players, as they could potentially amplify their calls for a PvP-free playlist.

Awards Season will be here before we know it, and there are already a few projects getting early buzz. One of them is the new A24 movie Club Kid, which stars Jordan Firstman, who also wrote and directed the acclaimed dramedy. Club Kid is my favorite movie of the year, largely thanks to its heart and the authentic representation of queer nightlife. I had to ask him about bringing those sequences together, and he got honest about why the club scenes (especially in the darkroom) went so hard.

Club Kid is a new LGBTQ+ movie, and as a gay man myself I was immediately take by how real those club scenes felt. As you can see in the video above, I asked Firstman about how he brought those sequences together, especially the scene where his character Peter has sex with a woman in a club darkroom. He told me:

I got in like a fight with someone because they're like 'Darkrooms like didn't come until like 2019.' And I was like, 'They definitely came in 2016.' I like remember like at least they were popping up in New York, but I remember going to like a sex party in 2015 or 16. But I say like the Berlin-ification of New York, mama, in the movie. But I do feel like, you know, Chris Cruse started this party Spotlight in LA, which was kind of like our first like LA introduction into darkrooms. It was a cool moment for queer people because we like weren't like doing that publicly before really in my generation. So yeah, it was important for me to like show that and show what goes down at the club

For those unfamiliar, darkrooms have a long history in queer history. They're typically pitch black rooms in bars where patrons can engage in anonymous sexual activity. They were shown in the media dating back to Harvey Fierstein's Torch Song Trilogy back in 1988, and Jordan Firstman's movie brings them back to the big screen in a more modern context.

In a drug-fueled haze Peter has sex with a woman early in Club Kid in a darkroom, and that unknowingly gets her pregnant. That's how his son Arlo ends up dropped at his door over a decade later, with the party promoter suddenly forced to become a parent to a child he never knew existed.

There's been a ton of chatter lately about LGBTQ+ movies actually starring queer actors, and Jordan Firstman was able to bring a very real, niche experience to the mainstream as the director, writer, and star of Club Kid. Later in our conversation he spoke more about the way the darkroom scene was shot, telling me:

But I think also showing it in a elegant way, like I really love how that scene is shot. I think it's like very classy. And it's not, it's like, I don't know. It just it's like beautiful, but still it does, a dark room does feel that way.

He's not wrong. The darkroom scene isn't a sexually explicit scene, despite the setting. Instead it uses light in a fascinating way that's immersive, but not overly graphic. The audience sees Peter decide to have sex with a woman at the behest of a guy he's interested in, and it's that union that serves as the catalyst for the movie's primary story.

The authentic way the darkroom is shown, as well as the unique chaos of the nightlife as a whole, instantly brings Club Kid into a specific time and place. The movie shows what the club scene is like for LGBTQ+ folks, warts and all. While it's a world not all moviegoers might understand, the specificity of Firstman's work ends up making the story universal.

Club Kid is in select theaters now as part of the 2026 movie release list, and will be getting more screenings as the month goes on. I laughed, I cried, and I loved how real the movie felt as a member of the queer community.

#3794. GTA 6 reportedly has 55 Achievements/Trophies, more than both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 had at launch

GTA 6 is due to release on the 19th November on PS5, and Xbox Series X/S, and ahead of the highly-anticipated launch of Rockstar's latest sandbox adventure, people just can't get enough information about the game. To that end, overnight, we saw our latest leak: the game will have 55 Trophies/Achievements.

In a now-deleted tweet from (in)famous Rockstar dataminer, TexFunz2 - re-posted by the Twitter account iGrandTheftAuto - it appears the game will have 55 individual rewards for completing certain tasks and missions. At the time of writing, we don't know specifically what these challenges are, but it seems none of them will be attached to the online version of the game; the base game launches without GTA Online, and so we can safely assume that all these rewards will be for the single-player only content. GTA Online will drop sometime in 2027, according to Twitch's CEO.

If you've been paying attention to previous Rockstar titles, you'll know that Grand Theft Auto 5 launched with 51 Achievements/Trophies - again, all single-player - and Red Dead Redemption 2 launched with 52. So the latest game has more than either game got at launch - and I can tell you from experience, getting Platinum in either title was a very time-consuming experience. Expect the same to be true here, too.

It's worth highlighting that GTA 5 did, eventually, get more Achievements and Trophies: the GTA Online content upped the complete total to 78, adding 27 new challenges to complete. I would expect GTA 6 to do the same… whenever the PC version of GTA comes out, or GTA Online lands in the new game (it's possible both could happen at the same time).

Recently, we heard why a former Rockstar Games tech director thinks GTA 6 could be coming to PC sooner than you'd expect (mostly thanks to AI clones), when we can expect the pre-load of the game (10th November), and how big the final game install is expected to be (210GB). The final game is expected to be so big and dense with detail that no single Rockstar employee has seen the entire game, meaning there are plenty of easter eggs and ridiculous things to discover.
