With Jensen Huang stepping down from Nvidia amid a second affair allegation coming yesterday, Nvidia will be looking for a new permanent CEO, with Interim CEO Colette Kress taking over for now. There will no doubt be lots of names thrown out over the coming weeks, and current US President Donald Trump has joined the pile, insisting the AI company hire ex-Apple CEO Tim Cook.

Taking to Truth Social, he says, "NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!"

Tim Cook became the CEO of Apple on August 24, 2011, famously taking over for Steve Jobs, the founder of the company. Tim Cook stepped away from his seat as CEO in August, 2026, but has stayed on as the Executive Chairman of Apple.

Tim Cook and Donald Trump have had a longstanding professional relationship, with the ex-Apple CEO reportedly donating $1 million to the Trump inauguration. Trump brought both Jensen Huang and Tim Cook on his trip to China earlier this year, where they had negotiations with the Chinese government to open up trade relations in regard to AI hardware. This was the first presidential trip to China since Trump's first visit back in 2017.

Whether or not the 66-year-old ex-Apple CEO is the right man for the job, his relationship with Trump is undeniable, and they both seem intent on growing AI in America and supplying more (but a limited amount of) AI to China.

Nvidia is a company that owes its sudden net worth explosion to the widespread adoption of AI. It went from a company with a market cap of hundreds of billions in 2020 to a company with a market cap of trillions in 2026. It saw a stock dip this morning, but even at its lowest stock price in more than a year, the company's market cap is still close to $4 trillion. Apple, too, has grown significantly and is currently the most highly valued company in the world.

Tim Cook is just one of many names tipped to take over as CEO in the future, with some Nvidia staff such as current CTO Michael Kagan among them. But, as far as external candidates are concerned, one might consider Intel's CEO Lip-Bu Tan, AMD's CEO, Lisa Su, Arm's CEO Rene Haas or even Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk as potential candidates. The doors really are wide open.

#3791. Dungeons in World of Warcraft: Forever get a huge XP buff, but power-levellers shouldn't celebrate just yet

World of Warcraft: Forever has received a massive buff to the XP drop-rates of dungeon mobs (enemies), which should make running these instances multiple times feel more rewarding - and may revive an older levelling strategy.

This buff is a 50 percent increase in experience from all mobs killed inside all dungeons. As detailed in this World of Warcraft forum post, community manager Kaivax wrote that this change has been made "so it feels better to go back in for more runs". They don't outright say this is in response to community feedback, but the subject has been a hot topic since the beta.

World of Warcraft: Forever developers have spoken in the past about the decision to deliberately bring down dungeon mob XP to disincentivise power-levelling in dungeons. The idea was that by doing this, people would be encouraged to actually go out into the world and explore it, rather than hopping from instance to instance until they reached max level.

Sadly, a side effect of this change is that doing a dungeon more than once could feel unrewarding. Playing it once is great, as you get to complete lots of quests that reward guaranteed items and XP. However, if you go back again, you don't get these, so your only source of progression comes from a heavily decreased XP rate.

Some quests exacerbate this issue. Dungeons like Wailing Caverns and especially Blackfathom Deeps have a quest that can't really be completed in one run due to a reliance on drop rates for items you need, and having to fight for drops with the rest of your dungeon party. Having to go back to complete this used to suck, and now it sucks less!

So does this mean farming dungeons to power-level is back? Maybe, but it still won't be nearly as efficient as it was in older versions of Classic WoW. The current mob XP rates, after this buff, will still only be 36 percent of the original Classic rate - a third. Given how fast you can level by doing quests out in the world, it seems dungeon farming isn't due for a comeback just yet.

After an especially smooth launch, World of Warcraft: Forever has become the biggest launch in the series' history, beating out Wrath of the Lich King, Cataclysm, and all the other past expansion launches. The developers have been quick to hotfix things on the fly, including a change that left PvP battlegrounds heavily advantaged for the Horde.

Spoilers for Season 3 of Nobody Wants This are ahead! Read at your own risk, and stream the series with a Netflix subscription.

Season 3 of Nobody Wants This was all about Joanne and Noah getting engaged and eventually married amid Joanne converting to Judaism. However, I’d argue that Sasha and Morgan’s story, and specifically Sasha’s whole situation with her and Esther, played an equally important and big role in this installment that dropped on the 2026 TV schedule. Now, as the series prepares to go into Season 4, two of the stars joked about Timothy Simons, who plays Sasha, taking over as the lead. However, here’s the thing: I actually think that should happen.

Now, I’ll admit it, my worst Nobody Wants This fear had to do with Sasha and Morgan getting together. However, when it happened in Season 3, I couldn’t deny how entertaining their arc was. Specifically, their episode in New York is a standout of the season, and that’s what began this conversation that led to a joke about Simons leading the show. Here’s what Joanne actress Kristen Bell had to say about Morgan and Sasha's trip to the Big Apple during an FYC event in LA (via THR):

The whole New York episode I think is one of the best episodes of television that has ever been made. I was standing up watching the cut.

Bell also said that her “body was aching for them to be together.” Meanwhile, Justine Lupe, who plays Morgan, said she was “live texting” Timothy Simons about “how hot” he was in the episode. That’s how we get to this idea of making Sasha the lead of Nobody Wants This, because the Frozen actress said:

I was like, ‘You guys, Tim is a romantic lead.’ I said it, everyone’s gonna know it. We’re gonna need security on set next year. He’s the lead of the show now — somebody’s gotta tell Adam [Brody].

Again, while I don’t really want Morgan and Sasha to be endgame, and I often have weird feelings about their romantic relationship, I see the potential here. Their chemistry is undeniable, they are so funny together, and their friendship is genuinely so special. Meanwhile, Sasha’s whole situation with Esther, especially now that she knows about what happened in New York, ups the drama exponentially. To me, the story writes itself, and it’d make perfect sense if Sasha’s love life became the focal point of Nobody Wants This.

Plus, Joanne and Noah are married. Their origin story is done. They’re an established couple, and while I always want to see them, their romance feels like it won’t (and probably shouldn’t) feature the drama it did in earlier seasons. So, by making Sasha the lead, they can stay a happy couple, while he dives into the drama of figuring out his marriage with Esther and his relationship with Morgan.

So, now that we know Season 4 of Nobody Wants This is coming, I hope this dream becomes a reality. Sasha is such a wonderful character, he’s in quite the mess with Morgan and Esther, and I’m certain that his love life would make for a brilliant season of TV. So, let’s make it happen.

#3784. "Art, including characters, terrain, animations, cutscenes and UI" Bandai Namco and Monolith Soft helped out with Ocarina of Time on Switch 2

Xenoblade series developer Monolith Soft and Bandai Namco Studios have been listed as support studios for the Switch 2 version of Ocarina of Time, working on elements of the title such as "art, including characters, terrain, animations, cutscenes and UI". Special thanks to both companies appear in the credits for the newly-launched game (as you can see below) and a statement released by Bandai Namco Studios confirms its involvement, too.

"We were commissioned to produce some of the visual assets and artwork, including characters, environments, animations, cutscenes, and UI elements, for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, a Nintendo Switch 2 game released by Nintendo Co., Ltd. on 5th November, 2026," reads a translated release from Bandai Namco Studio reads.

Of course, this isn't the first time we've seen Bandai Namco Studios' talents leveraged to help with Nintendo games: the publisher and its internal studios worked closely with Nintendo as a co-developer on the long-awaited Metroid Prime 4, and we know the studios are listed as co-developer for first-party Switch 2 titles like Mario Kart World and Splatoon Raiders. Typically, the work carried out by Bandai Namco comes from one of two dedicated internal studios that are contracted specifically to work with Nintendo: Studio 2 and Studio S. You can see a full list of the games Bandai Namco's support studios have worked on here. You'll note there are many Nintendo first-party titles listed here, going back to 2012 and Mario Kart 8. In late 2025, Nintendo acquired Bandai Namco Studios Singapore from the publisher, renaming the company Nintendo Studios Singapore.

"Alongside great judgement and clever tweaks, this astonishing remake has a proper ace up its sleeve," wrote our reviewer, Christian Donlan, in his five-star review of the Switch 2 game last week. "This is Ocarina as it's always been, as timeless and intricate, but it also has a vibrancy and clarity that makes it feel like it was just created last Wednesday."

If - somehow! - you've already gobbled up most of the game and you're keen to play it again, you will be pleased to know that Master Quest code has been found in datamined files for the title, suggesting DLC may well be on the way in the not-too-distant future.

#3783. Skyrim lead designer hopes Sentinel will finally solve The Elder Scrolls' ladder problem

For such a simple, straightforward real-world object, ladders have been the bane of game developers' existence since the early days of the industry. And Bethesda's The Elder Scrolls Series is certainly no stranger to that struggle.

While we may be years away from the release of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, the recent title reveal reignited conversations about what longtime fans hope to see from it. That includes former Bethesda developers, such as Skyrim lead designer and Bethesda veteran Bruce Nesmith, who picked ladders as one thing he hopes Sentinel actually figures out.

If you're unfamiliar, ladders in Skyrim work in a weird way. You don't animatedly climb up and down them, but rather the character simply teleports from one end to the other. Speaking to The Examined Game (via GamesRadar+), Nesmith said that Skyrim's approach "really limits the art team in terms of how you can do multi-layer [levels]".

"It seems simple, it seems stupid, but you don't climb up and down ladders," said Nesmith. "All the ladders in Skyrim, you click on the ladder, poof, you're at the top or you have to climb a stair.

"But to do ladders, you have to deal with a whole host of questions which our programmers very legitimately put in front of us and said, 'You give me answers to these, I'll tell you how much programming time it's going to take to make them.' And you know, that caused problems right there."

Nesmith then pointed out the hidden complexity of creating functioning ladders in games, and the scenarios developers have to anticipate and account for, especially in a game as dynamic as an Elder Scrolls title.

"So, I'm halfway up a ladder, and [an] NPC decides to climb down it. What happens?" Nesmith posited. "The NPC has to have AI that will adjust for that. Does the player go through the NPC? Is he blocked by the NPC? Does the NPC stay on the ladder? Does the NPC go back up and know to wait and then come back down?

"And I'm just scratching the surface of some of the problems they brought up. So, it seems simple, and other games have climbing ladders, but we chose to put our efforts into other things to make them better rather than deal with that. So, I'd like to see Bethesda finally come around to making ladders a reality where you're actually climbing them and make the world feel a little more immersive."

While we know very little about Sentinel right now - much less how it's going to solve the ladder problem -that hasn't stopped fans from speculating about a number of topics, including what they believe is going to be a split / alternate timeline setup.

When you’re lucky enough to have the kind of successful career that Daniel Radcliffe has had, adoring fans come with the territory. Of course, the 37-year-old will always be the original Harry Potter (even though the new series is coming quickly on the 2026 TV schedule), and he’ll always have people quoting the Harry Potter movies and books to him. The actor was just asked about that experience, and his answer lines up with Keira Knightley’s take on it.

Radcliffe was just asked if there’s a quote from one of his movies that’s recited to him the most during an interview with People. Here’s what he had to say:

Unless you’re doing a very obvious one to me now, it will go over my head. You do a deep cut Harry Potter line to me, I’ll probably look at you very blankly right now, because it’s been a long time.

So, if you’re hoping to impress Radcliffe by quoting something from one of his roles, as he says, it probably will go past him very easily. And to be fair, much of his most famous work was filmed when he was growing up. It’d be like asking someone to remember what you said in class in fifth grade once. Here’s what Keira Knightley said to Heart on the same topic just the other day:

I have not watched Love Actually since the premiere, which was when I was 18. So, I think I’m the person that knows it the least of anybody. I know that people have a particular look on their face and then they say things to me and I know that means they’re quoting Love Actually, but I don’t really know what it is. It means nothing to me.

Wild, right? It’s like everyone knows their most famous work except for them. In Knightley’s defense, she also said she was on the set of Love Actually for a week. And now it’s considered one of the best Christmas movies.

Hey, I wouldn’t rewatch my 18-year-old self either! But it’s still pretty crazy that she has managed to only see it once, considering its widespread popularity. It’s funny that she can tell when people are probably quoting something at her, but she doesn’t quite know what to do or what movie or TV show they are talking about.

While Daniel Radcliffe isn’t going to get most of the Harry Potter quotes you might throw his way, he did point out one he’ll probably get. In his words:

But, I suppose it would be, ‘You’re a wizard, Harry.’ But like, no one’s said that for a long time to be honest. So yeah, I don’t know, but that’s a classic. That one I would be like, ‘That’s from Harry Potter. I recognize that.’

That’s a softball one, for sure. I mean, if he didn’t get that one, I would be a little bit worried about the guy to be honest.

Anyways, it’s definitely an understandable take from both of them, considering they've been working since they were kids and have both dealt with mass fame for most of their lives. It wouldn’t be healthy if they knew every line of their projects either, would it?

These days, Daniel Radcliffe has his own comedy series in The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins and is one of the leading voice stars of Netflix’s new animated movie, Steps, coming out on November 20. Whereas Keira Knightley has just returned to her well-reviewed thriller series, Black Doves for Season 2, which is streaming on Netflix now. I guess you know what to do if you happen to cross paths with them… maybe don’t confuse them with deep-cut quotes you've memorized.

#3780. Nintendo's legendary Kirby designer Masahiro Sakurai weighs in on gen-AI, saying "it has yet to gain my trust" but not to reject it completely

"Doing nothing is probably not the right approach."

Masahiro Sakurai, the designer behind many iconic Nintendo franchises such as Super Smash Bros. and several Kirby titles, has weighed in on the ongoing discussion of generative-AI use in game development.

At an event celebrating the release of his new book - Masahiro Sakurai’s Thoughts on Games - the veteran director told Famitsu he hasn't and currently isn't using the technology to make games, noting that the role of a designer is to generate ideas.

"It has yet to gain my trust," Sakurai said via DeepL machine translation. Regarding graphical use specifically, he added that, "It must not amount to exploitation of any kind," and that "for the time being, we can produce better results by coming up with ideas ourselves".

But Sakurai is wary of rejecting gen-AI completely, saying "making games today is far too difficult", with some games "running at a loss even after selling millions of copies". A company in that position may go under if it does not change its stance on generative-AI, he suggested. "Doing nothing is probably not the right approach," he said, but "where and how to use it" is a complex topic with a lot of uncertainties. Sakurai is taking "a slow-paced approach" for now.

Outside of regular industry layoffs, the use of generative-AI in games has been the most controversial topic amongst developers and players. Some argue it's already being used in multiple development disciplines, notably programming and writing code. Others, such as Shigeru Miyamoto, are more sceptical of the technology's capabilities, especially when it comes to the more creative and art-driven parts of game development.

#3777. NVIDIA CEO resigns amid infidelity scandal, Chinese spy accusations

There's a lot going on in tech these days, eh/

NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has resigned effective immediately amid concerns about several extramarital affairs, including one with someone who’s suspected to be a Chinese spy.

An investigation is ongoing when it comes to the latter, but for now, Huang has stepped down and been replaced by Colette Kress, NVIDIA’s current executive vice president and chief financial officer in an interim basis.

“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Kress in a statement. “We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.”

Unsurprisingly, NVIDIA stock dropped about 23 percent this morning as concerns about the company’s stability expectedly linger, on top of a massive plunge in AI stocks last week in the wake of the US elections.

“Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” said Harvey Jones, Chair of the NVIDIA Board of Directors, of the interim CEO. “She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing NVIDIA’s strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.”

How will this affect gamers? It’s unclear for now, but the balance of power in the tech industry could shift towards other companies powering the AI bubble, like AMD and OpenAI. Either way, pardon my lack of optimism that this is going to change anything or make the price of GPUs suddenly drop to an affordable rate.

Update on Nov. 12 at 2:40pm CT: Reuters is reporting a third affair for Huang, this one another employee who works at NVIDIA. Stay tuned, the numbers could climb as high as GPU prices.

#3776. Activision cracking down on popular Call of Duty: Warzone app that basically constituted cheating

"Lobby shopping" is what Call of Duty: Warzone players have been calling the ability to check the skill level of players in a lobby prior to joining it, enabling them to pass on those that include a lot of tough competition.

There are several ways players, notably Twitch streamers and content creators, have been able to do that over the years. But the use of one app in particular - Warzone Agent - has been considered by many to be cheating, and Activision is finally doing something about it.

Alongside the launch of Modern Warfare 4's version of Warzone and the game's first season of post-launch content, Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet has announced it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

"Yesterday, we began taking action against Warzone Agent, a paid, unauthorised third party tool that lets users lobby shop in Warzone," the developer revealed in a post on X. "Ricochet anti-cheat will block players attempting to load the software and instruct them to unload it before accessing multiplayer."

Having the ability to cherrypick the lobby with the lowest-skilled players possible bypasses the game's matchmaking algorithm, potentially ruining the game for the dozens of other players in the match. Historically, content creators have used the app (and other methods) to post impressive kill records.

The developer added in a follow-up message that: "Using unauthorised software to manipulate the player experience violates Activision terms of use and leaves your account and hardware subject to enforcement." The language seems to stop just short of outright confirming those players using Warzone Agent will be banned.

As part of this crackdown, Ricochet reiterated its stance on boosting - artificially increasing (or decreasing) one's skill rating - saying that it too is considered cheating. "Receiving a boost, having another player log in to boost your account, or purchasing a boosted account are all against policy," the developer said.

"Boosting services flood lobbies with low effort accounts used to farm XP and complete challenges. Those accounts can later be sold as Ranked Play ready, directly feeding the cheating marketplace."

More than 20,000 boosting-related accounts have been removed since the launch of Modern Warfare 4, according to the developer, and Ricochet will "continue to apply pressure" in this area.

The quality of multiplayer was a particular highlight in Eurogamer's review of Modern Warfare 4, in which Dom Peppiatt lauded the complexity of weapon handling, which works without taking away from accessibility of the gunplay.

With Jensen Huang gone, someone has to fill his boots. That's Kress, for the time being.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Jensen Huang has resigned, and in his place is a familiar face for anyone that's listened to one of Nvidia's financial calls: it's the company's long-standing CFO, Colette Kress.

But you might be excused as a gamer for never hearing about her; an earnings call isn't everybody's cup of tea.

Colette Kress has been chief financial officer at Nvidia since 2013. That's 13 years sat alongside Jensen in calls with investors and financial institutions to discuss how the company is doing. Kress has been in the role for the record highs of recent years, and the not-so-record lows of others, like the price plummets of '25, '21, and '18.

Prior to her role at Nvidia, Kress was SVP and CFO at Cisco for a couple of years and Corporate VP at Microsoft for nearly five. She also worked at Texas Instruments—all the big hitters, then.

Generally, Kress has stayed out of any contentious issues with the company, only occassionally commenting on the big issues during earnings calls. Like when the RTX 30-series was out of stock everywhere thanks to cryptocurrency mining (the mining had an impact on the company's financials in a slightly contentious way, too).

Or ceaseless comments on the increasing demand for AI datacentre build out. That's of less interest to gamers, but what do you expect? Nvidia to talk about gaming GPUs in this day and age? It cannot be done.

In an email to employees in the wake of Jensen Huang's departure, Kress reportedly said (via Hadas Gold on X):

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

"I believe deeply in this company and in its future. More than anything, I believe in each of you, in our customers and partners and in the vital role we play every day in the global economy.

"The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication. Thank you.

"... We play a vital role in building the technology that is powering the AI revolution, and we have important work ahead of us. So let's move forward together, with the same determination and commitment that have always defined this company."

Here are the emails sent to Nvidia employees: Company meeting Nov 18 https://t.co/9X67XzSOCeNovember 12, 2026

Kress also notes there will be a company meeting on November 18—the day after Nvidia's next financial call, which Kress will have been preparing for in her CFO role, and the day of Jensen Huang's meeting with US House leaders.

Kress will have been chosen for this interim CEO role in some part to steady the markets. It takes a long time to find and finalise a deal to secure a new full-time CEO, especially with a job opening as internationally as important as this one. So someone inside the company had to take the chalice for now. With Kress at the helm, Nvidia will be hoping investors won't be quite as worried about the company's financial future.

It's the same playbook we saw when Intel ousted then-CEO Brian Krzanich over a consensual relationship he had with an employee, which was against company policy. Krzanich was replaced by Bob Swan as interim CEO, who actually took over as CEO at a later date, before Pat Gelsinger took over from him in 2021. Pat then retired in 2024.

Nvidia will likely look at this as a bit of a cautionary tale: you want stability and leadership, not a revolving door of top execs and no one steering the ship. If the board has any wits about it, it'll be looking for a strong leader with a clear direction for the company and the will to deliver it.

President Donald Trump has come out in support of a man who only just managed to escape top corporate life at Apple: Tim Cook.

Meanwhile the China Select Committee in US Congress backs any leader that "makes national security its top priority."

So, a true patriot that can also lead teams of top-class engineers and wants to fill the boots of a man that famously didn't take breaks. That'll be easy to find, I'm sure.

#3774. Resident Evil Requiem kicks award season off with series of sweeps, but it’s on a collision course with GTA for the crown jewels

Resident Evil Requiem has kicked off the awards season by securing several major awards for itself, including the Ultimate Game of the Year given out by the Golden Joysticks. It was also the best console game of 2026 and won an award for the best trailer, while Angela Sant’Albano, who plays Grace Ashcroft, earned due recognition for her performance.

With RE9, Capcom spearheaded itself to the top of the gaming world, receiving a Studio of the Year award, among others, totaling seven accolades from the Golden Joysticks alone. More are bound to follow, not least because the one big game still remaining doesn’t qualify for most award shows anyway. Resident Evil Requiem is thus the supergiant bent on conquering every award out there, but one may yet escape its grasp.

I am talking, of course, about The Game Awards’ prestigious Game of the Year trophy, which to some extent stands on par with The Academy’s Oscars in our industry. Every year, one game and studio gets to take home the biggest win, and while I would love to see RE9 or The Blood of Dawnwalker developers walk down those steps holding a winged statue, I have a feeling that the chugging hype train building around GTA 6 might put a full stop on those dreams.

So far, TGA has held its ground against community hype, allocating most of the ultimate decision to the jury rather than the players, who, though they can pick their player choice award, still don’t have too much of an impact on who gets the Game of the Year accolade. Back in 2013, while it was still rather in its infancy, TGA did not give GTA 5 a GOTY award, and it actually snubbed Red Dead Redemption in favor of the rebooted God of War. So far, Rockstar hasn’t had much luck with Geoff Keighley’s show, but it also hasn’t had a game as hyped-up and anticipated as GTA 6 in its history, despite the gargantuan size of each of its IPs.

Whether Keighley and his show can withstand that onslaught remains to be seen, but I, for one, think that GTA 6 might have already been chosen for that silver trophy, and since we know for a fact that juries probably don’t play much of the games they ultimately settle on, I believe this one is already set in stone. And that, unfortunately, means someone has to lose and miss out, in this case Capcom’s fantastic set of 2026 heavy-hitters from Resident Evil 9 to Pragmata to Onimusha: Way of the Sword.

#3773. Rockstar's doing a GTA 6 launch 'festival' in Miami featuring a lot of presumably expensive musical stars

The next-level glamour of Grand Theft Auto 6's arrival continues with word that Rockstar is hosting a star-studded launch 'festival' for the game in Miami - the game's setting-by-a-different-name.

The event will feature two stages hosting live performances by musical artists both featured in the game and from those who are not. Cardi B is probably the headliner - my knowledge of popular music is creaking here - but there's also Travis Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black, Sofaygo, Ca7riel, and Paco Amoroso.

Meanwhile, GTA 6 soundtrack duo Justice are doing a DJ set, as are The Dare with Fcukers, which is a dangerous name to spell. Also appearing: Metro Boomin, Nick León with DJ Python, Propsa with Skream, Rauw and Friends, Suero, and Tainy.

The event is being hosted at event space Mana Wynwood, and the pre-sale lottery for tickets begins this week on Wednesday, 11th November. Tickets are limited to two a head.

The full soundtrack for GTA 6 is yet to be revealed, with only a handful of songs so far detailed - featuring Rauw, Ca7riel, Paco Amoroso, and Travis Scott, among others. But of course music and radio stations play a huge role in the series, and given the amount of time we'll be playing GTA 6 and listening to these songs, it may well provide a lucrative platform to be featured on.

Meanwhile, the cultural impact of GTA 6's imminent arrival continues with a takeover of swanky department store Selfridges in London, which has a custom Ferrari parked in a window and an extensive range of expensive merch to buy.

It's not all good news for Rockstar, though. The company is also fighting an employment tribunal in Scotland relating to the sudden firing of 31 staff from Rockstar North this time last year. Rockstar alleges this was done for gross misconduct reasons, whereas the fired staff maintain it was done in the name of union busting. The results of that hearing are expected close to GTA 6's release, on 19th November.

The romance is great, but the emotional depth is better.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Wicker has been advertised as an extremely sexually charged movie with a hot man made of wicker. The film doesn’t shy away from sex and sexuality. It has a few very fun sex scenes that a lot of hard work went into. I wasn’t sure what to expect going into Wicker beyond some raunchiness.

I was delighted to discover it's far more complex than it's promoted. It touches upon topics of self-esteem in really haunting and interesting ways.

Warning: Wicker spoilers are ahead. Proceed with caution.

Fisherwoman (Olivia Colman) has always been an outcast in her town. They tease and treat her as if her only purpose is to sell them fish. She has no real friends and not much of a romantic prospect. This led the Fisherwoman to accept a lonely life. She finally decides to change that, but the scars remain from being told that she doesn’t deserve good things, especially a man who loves her.

The Fisherwoman has a lot of trauma and self-esteem issues from years of being told by society that she’s not worthy of happiness. However, she isn’t the only one with society-based scars. All the women in town have them. This is why the Wicker Husband (Alexander Skarsgård) is so attractive to many women. He doesn’t operate with the same rules of this society.

He loves deeply and purely, without constraining how his wife should live. Sadly, this nonconforming spirit also makes the Fisherwoman doubt his love and fidelity. She has seen the men of this society. She finds it hard to believe that she has one who respects and loves her.

I left Wicker very annoyed with the Fisherwoman. She almost killed her husband because of a lie. Additionally, she refused to believe him, even though he has only ever been honest. It’s also clear that he only exists for her. I was shouting, “Be reasonable, woman!” as she behaved in unreasonable ways.

However, then I had to think about how many women and men let their lack of self-esteem or past trauma ruin good things in their lives. Many relationships have been destroyed because one or both people in them let their insecurities grow and create bigger problems. The Fisherwoman is frustrating, but she’s very human.

I really enjoyed the Wicker ending because everyone got what they deserved. The townsfolk got scammed and traumatized. The Butcher (Phil Daniels ) got murdered, as the worst husband of them all, and the Fisherwoman and Wicker Husband left with a new child.

It was only after the Fisherwoman could let go of her insecurities and her awful town that she could have a happy ending. Wicker is about letting love into your life, even when you don’t think you deserve it.

The Fisherwoman creates a husband who loves her completely, but she also learns to love herself in the process. That’s the real message. Find love within yourself, and the right person may find you, or you will at least love yourself enough to feel fulfilled with or without a partner. Wicker is definitely worth seeing in a theater full of women, or alone, where you can meditate on its messages.

Either way, come for the sexy parts, stay for the self-love.

#3771. Probably Stolen Lou quest walkthrough: How to complete and all rewards

The game’s most wanted criminal, no NPC in Probably Stolen can rival or challenge the mysterious (& dangerous) Lou.

And as you can expect, her cryptic persona persists in her quest, which can only be triggered and completed by playing a dangerous game. Here’s a full walkthrough on how to complete the Lou storyline in Probably Stolen.

Unlike most NPCs, like Serpico and Eleanor, Lou only appears on a random day after you purchase the Business Permit, available in the fifth week. During her visit, she will introduce herself before asking you for a series of ”tools” to be used on her next job. To trigger her quest and start her storyline, call Security on her and claim the 1.500 Credits bounty.

Now that you surprised Lou and made the questionable choice of turning in a specialist, a Republic Operative will pay you a visit in the next week, claiming Lou to be a traitor to the Republic and an alleged terrorist. He also gives you a Republic Transmitter and makes an offer: plant it into something and give it to Lou for 700 Credits, as she is sure to visit you again.

Sure enough, Lou will surprise you in a few weeks, inviting you to play a game and letting you know what’s at stake. The next morning, she reveals that a bomb is hidden within your wares and gives you until midnight to disarm it. Upon review, the Plastic Explosive will prove to be fake.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Following your fake brush with death, Lou will pay a visit to the store in around five days and leave her ”Box of Toys” in your care, before warning you not to touch it. The box features a document revealing more about her past and ties with the Republic.

She returns to grab it the next day. If you haven’t moved the contents of the box (you can still read the document at no risk) or placed the transmitter in it, she allows you to pick either 1x Advanced Turbo Booster, 1x Smuggler’s Bay, 1x Backpack (Small), or 2x Module Expansion Kits as a reward.

Following the encounter above, just keep playing until Lou visits under the guise of an inspector. She reveals that her ”guest’ has finally given her the info she needs, before asking for 750 Credits (or 500 depending on your chosen difficulty) worth of weapons, armor, or meds as a trade for the bounty you received earlier. You have one week to secure it. If you can’t, she asks for the amount in Credits on the due date.

We are now at the final stretch of her storyline, as Lou will thank you and vanish upon getting the agreed-upon ”tools” (or the necessary Credits) in her next visit. This will be your final meeting, with the news of the assassination of an admiral stamping the papers the next morning. She will send you a note, though, together with a Storage Bay Expansion Kit.

Lou’s quest/storyline then ends with another visit from the Republic Operative, who reveals they plan to pursue her and hints at your involvement in the whole ordeal.

With Lou’s quest done, don’t forget to also check out how to produce Huge Nutrifruits and unlock the Green Thumb achievement.

#3770. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang under investigation after admitting affair with alleged Chinese spy in company-wide email

"There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

Nvidia's board of directors has launched an investigation into its own CEO Jensen Huang, after a report by the New York Times claimed he had been participating in an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Huang admitted to having an affair in a company-wide statement, apologising to his wife as well as to Nvidia employees. Following this acknowledgement, independent investigators are looking into whether or not he's been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

Per the New York Times article, the alleged spy was named as Megaspeed executive and Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang or Huang Le. Jensen Huang wrote in his internal letter: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

With regard to security concerns surrounding the CEO of US-based company Nvidia potentially sharing information with a spy, Huang confirmed that the Nvidia board of directors had initiated an investigation. He added: "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully." The Nvidia board has said it has "no reason to believe either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."

Huang will remain CEO of Nvidia while the investigation is conducted. The New York Times report also claimed that US government officials did not believe Huang knew of Alice Huang's alleged intelligence activities for China.

Following the internal letter from Jensen Huang, Nvidia stock took a tumble from $162bn to $150bn. Nvidia, a juggernaut in the video game hardware industry, is also a key player in the global generative AI industry, which is currently carrying the US economy as other sectors struggle. The company is responsible for AI technology like DLSS 5, which generates lighting, shadows and more using generative AI.

Concerns around the Chinese AI sector passing the American industry has been a core argument against AI development slowdown or regulation, and it's also why Huang's affair may be a matter of national interest.

#3769. Ball x Pit’s Risen Ballbylon DLC is a ball-bustingly difficult good time, and just as cheap

Ball x Pit was one of my top indie titles of 2025, and its balls have been buffed several times over since then with free updates.

But now, a paid DLC has hit Ballbylon, and at $6.99, it’s worth every penny so long as you can withstand the ball-busting difficulty. The Risen Ballbylon expansion is here, and it takes the fight above as opposed to below as you ascend in your elevator to find new enemies, riches, and biomes to explore.

I can’t overstate the value that this DLC brings for just a few bucks. Four new biomes/stages, eight new playable characters, 24 new balls, 20 new ball evolutions, 20 new buildings, 46 new passive abilities…you get the picture. There’s a lot more Ball in here, and you need every bit of balls you have because this DLC is tough, which is to be expected considering it’s an endgame activity only available once you’ve completed the base game.

The ballbreaking begins with the first new stage, FLOODEDxSEWERS, which is filled with sharks and mermen and all sorts of other deep-sea-like creatures throwing spears at you, and never really slows down from there. Gathering the new playable characters is crucial, because they are indeed powerful, leaving a lot of the base game’s characters in the dust. But the progress is slow at first thanks to a new material that is hard to come by in the beginning: Crystals.

These Crystals are found within new levels, like gold and collectible power gems, but in scarce supply to begin with. These are needed to build basically all of the new buildings, but especially the houses that unlock the new playable Hunters. I think my favorite so far is the Wallbreaker, whose balls hit the wall and some come out the other side, making for some very fun geometry and wildness when baby balls start taking up the screen.

Your base will need to be fully upgraded from the jump, so if you’re like me and didn’t play too much New Game Plus or continue on the expansion after finishing the story, you may have some grinding to do early on because the new stages hit hard, and they hit you right in the balls.

Mastering the new ball abilities, and especially the new Hunters and their plethora of new passive abilities you can select on any given run, will be crucial for success. I’m still trying to grind my way through the levels, collecting crystals where I can, but it’s slow-going…and still just as fun as I remember Ball x Pit to be.

But really, at $6.99, this really is a no-brainer addition to your library if you even got the smallest amount of joy out of Ball x Pit when it launched last year. It’s just a whole lot more of the great base game, with a new challenge for those who are looking for it.

The only question that remains: do you have the balls required?

#3768. Anticipated Warhammer 40K tactical RPG Dark Heresy gets a release date

Owlcat Games has revealed a release date for its tactical role-playing sequel Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy. The game arrives 28th January, 2027 on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X. A Switch 2 release date will be provided "at a later date", a press release says.

Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy follows the good work laid down by Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader a couple of years ago. "Rogue Trader nails the 40k setting and provides an appropriately massive narrative filled with meaty tactical combat, though some bugs and poor performance hold it back," wrote Caeyln Ellis in Eurogamer's Warhammer 40,000 Rogue Trade review.

Dark Heresy changes things by casting you as an Inquisitor and tasking you with hunting down heretics and purging the world of dark influences, as one is wont to do in the 41st century, it seems. And developer Owlcat has apparently overhauled many of the systems underpinning the adventure.

There's a beta that's been running for a while that offers a complete first Act to try, and it's accessible if you buy a Founders edition of the game. This beta, incidentally, disappears 7th January, when Owlcat prepares the game for launch.

Meanwhile, Owlcat is making a substantially different RPG based around the popular Expanse license - a game that's much more closely inspired by Mass Effect. That project recently recruited the help of former Dragon Age writer David Gaider, and it will no doubt hope to fill a much-lamented hole created recently by the cancellation of Mass Effect 5.

Grace and Bryan—two peas in a very scared pod.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Resident Evil Requiem's director, Koshi Nakanishi, once said that putting Leon Kennedy in a horror game simply wouldn't work because "he wouldn't jump at something like a bucket falling. No one wants to see Leon scared by everything". And he was right, I couldn't have felt safer with Leon in Requiem. Grace on the other hand, we were decidedly less safe in her hands.

But that didn't mean I enjoyed my time with her any less. While Leon's segments in Requiem were pure unbridled feel-good action, Grace found herself in one exhilaratingly stressful situation after another, not unlike another Resident Evil protagonist who rocked up this year. I'm of course talking about Bryan Hodukavich from Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie.

One of my favourite parts of the Resident Evil film was just how ordinary Bryan was, it not only made it infinitely scarier (especially the first part) but I felt empathy for this poor delivery driver in a way that I probably wouldn't for a trained bioweapon killing machine.

I hadn't actually thought about how alike Grace and Bryan are in this way, not until Grace's actress Angela Sant'Albano pointed it out herself during an interview with Radio Times Gaming.

"I thought the film was amazing," Sant'Albano says. "I'm a big Zach Cregger fan, I loved Weapons. I think what he's done is really brilliant and also, you know, their lead character is not Grace, but he is sort of an everyday person put in this extraordinary circumstance and I just think that really translates well to audiences. They want to feel like it could be them. So I'm a big fan of [Cregger] and always have been, and a big fan of the film."

It's certainly hard to be a fan of the games and not love Cregger's Resident Evil adaptation. I honestly don't think I've seen a better videogame adaptation, perhaps Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, but it's a close call. The only thing that would make Cregger's adaptation better in my books is if we somehow got to see Bryan cross paths with one of the videogame protagonists, but sadly that simply isn't possible—for many reasons.

#3766. Hollow Knight Silksong physical editions mention multiple "free content packs" incoming, and call Sea of Sorrow a "giant expansion"

More than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong are finally arriving on players' doorsteps. It's the same brilliant and sometimes thrillingly cruel Metroidvania Eurogamer gave five stars to, except this time a pack-in booklet seemingly reveals the existence of multiple "free content packs" alongside the Sea of Sorrow DLC.

Hollow Knight: Silksong's physical editions were originally set to be delivered from 10th November, but some early handovers have given us a peek inside the box. Redditor Me_975 posted pictures of their Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, and there's a few interesting tidbits tucked away - most notably in the manual's chapter on Content Packs.

"The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet reads. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with new friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!"

Developer Team Cherry confirmed plans for post-launch Silksong support last year, but remained pretty tight-lipped about what exactly that would look like. The indie outfit then announced the nautically themed Sea of Sorrow expansion, though we now have proper confirmation there's more content packs still to come, which shouldn't be a huge shocker considering all the free post-launch love Hollow Knight (the first one) received.

Speaking of Sea of Sorrow, that's mentioned here too: "In the first giant expansion, voyage across and beneath a salt-stricken ocean brimming with mystery and menace."

Sea of Sorrow's original release window was a vague 2026 - time's a-ticking, Team Cherry. Still no release date so far, but the booklet does say it's "Coming Soon." Of course, Team Cherry are quite infamous for working on games until they balloon wildly out of control. After all, Silksong was once upon a time intended to be a Hollow Knight DLC, but with games this detailed, I can't really complain about waiting a little extra.

If you are interested in owning Silksong physically, it comes with a big map of Pharloom and the rest of the booklet also includes some really lovely art seemingly ripped straight from the game, as well.

#3765. How to find a Guild in WoW Forever

No Guild Finder (so far) isn't stopping WoW: Forever players from finding (or even making) the perfect Guild

Guilds return in World of Warcraft: Forever, and Blizzard wants to recapture the excitement of hopping into the game and dragging your guildmates to the occasional raid, a good leveling session, or the plain old shenanigans. While guilds are already a staple in most MMOs and other versions of WoW, it’s still refreshing to see Forever return with a classic iteration of a staple social experience.

But since Forever is indeed a remake of Classic, it also comes with the sheer difficulty of finding a Guild you could be a part of. There’s really no way to tell if a Guild is available for applications, or maybe if a Guild is strictly friends-only. Then again, there are creative ways where you can score a Guild membership for your character.

Historically, WoW players have always been able to find Guilds through the Guild Finder, launched back in Cataclysm, as well as the improved Guild & Communities Finder back in 2019. Forever being a remake of the OG WoW means going back to a time where none of these tools existed, so it’s back to “manual” searching for WoW: Forever players.

As of writing, there are no WoW: Forever add-ons specifically to help find Guilds in the game. Sites like CurseForge do have a plethora of add-ons that help with Guild management, but that’s after you make your Guild.

Cataclysm launched the original Guild Finder back in 2011, so players had around seven years of finding guilds with no built-in tool to help them. Therefore, WoW: Forever players can also resort to old-fashioned ways of finding prospective Guilds.

Even without the Guild Finder, WoW: Forever players have a plethora of social avenues to form communities and find like-minded players for their Guilds. Forums and community messaging apps are perfect for guild recruitment, especially if they have dedicated group chats for Forever. Example avenues are:

Reddit and Discord are already great places to stay connected with fellow players or even get tips on things like PvP and builds, so it’s no surprise they are also great platforms to find Guilds to join.

There’s nothing wrong jumping to and from Guilds if you feel like the one you’re in doesn’t really suit your needs anymore. But to avoid those awkward situations when you do need to type “/gquit” in the chat, then remember these when joining:

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

Maybe you don’t want to be part of a Guild. Maybe you found some Guilds taking the game too seriously and you want something chill, or some Guilds might be “too” chill for your liking. That’s probably when you should consider making your own Guild.

If you want to create your own Guild, it has to be something certified by your Faction as 100% legit. This is quite unlike other MMOs where you can just make a Guild easy peasy, or just pay some currency to get the privilege. Instead, you need to get something called a Guild Charter.

To do this, head to your capital city. Ask a guard to help you locate your Guild Master. From here, you can ask them for a Guild Charter, and they’ll sell it to you for 10 Silver.

Be careful if you’re doing this purchase if you’re low-level, since that 10 Silver is already the current life savings of other characters. But once you’ve decided you really want to become a future guild founder, then proceed with the purchase and type in your Guild Name.

This won’t stop there, though. Before your Guild actually becomes legit, you need to find 10 Signatures first.

Unlike other MMOs, WoW: Forever takes a page from Classic’s rulebook and demands Signatures from other players to co-found your Guild. As with Classic, you also need 10 (!!!) Signatures in your Guild Charter. And if you’re not playing with friends who are ready to be your co-founders, it’s not easy to convince random people to just hop in and join someone’s Guild.

Once you find a player willing to help, you just right-click their name and ask them for their Signature. A prompt will appear on their end where they can sign your Guild Charter.

When you finally get your Signatures, you must rush back to your capital city and turn in the signed Guild Charter. Only then do you get your guild. But first things first, how exactly do you find Signatures?

Before you run off to Stormwind to grab that Guild Charter, just remember that creating a Guild in Forever does have its fair set of limitations. Huddle with your prospective guildmates and remember the following:

After you create your Guild, you practically have access to a mini-Faction within the Forever experience. As the leader, you (and a select few you appoint) have access to some of the Guild’s core settings. You can adjust these at any time, but the basics you should pay attention to are the following:

You might recall the suggestion to go to Discord to find a guild to join, or maybe even find potential guildmates. That’s because you can actually connect your WoW: Forever account to your Discord account as well. Doing this is pretty simple, and it’s all done from your settings:

First, you need to connect your Discord to your Battle.net account. To do this, go to your Discord account and click “User Settings.”

Under “Connected Apps,” you will see “Add a new connection,” and you can click the Battle.net icon there.

It will open Battle.net, where you can click “Continue,” and it will send you back to Discord, where you can “Authorize” the connection.

After that, you will be redirected to your settings, where you can confirm the connection.

Back in your WoW: Forever session, go to your “Options” and find “Social” under “Gameplay” or via the search.

It will show the Enable Discord Functionality toggle. Connect so you can link your Discord to your specific WoW account.

Below that setting is an option to choose how your name is displayed in the chat connected to Discord. It could be your Discord Global Name or your Last Online Character Name.

This part is best done if you’re the owner of the Guild, so you can set this up from scratch. Over in the “Guilds & Communities” tab, you can go to your “Guild Control” and check out Discord Settings.

From there, you can choose which Discord Server you want to connect to your Guild. And after that, you can select which specific channel you want to add to your Forever Guild.

When you link the two, the Discord channel overrides the Guild Chat by default. But there’s an option to separate the Discord chat as a separate channel from the Guild Chat.

Now, all your messages in WoW: Forever in that specific chat can be seen live on Discord. Likewise, messages from Discord will be seen back in WoW: Forever, with a nifty Discord icon to denote that the message has been sent from Discord specifically but read in-game.

While it’s possible to just separate your Discord chat from your Guild Chat, it might be economical to fix things over on Discord so that you have a dedicated guild channel for in-game players. You can lock that channel as view-only to non-players, so only guild members can actually chat there.

Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary from A24 about Elizabeth Holmes, You Can See Everything, is all about the truth. The central question that we, as the audience, are asking the entire time, who is telling the truth, who is lying, and just what is the truth. Even though Fielder spent weeks living with Holmes and her partner just prior to the former Theranos founder reporting to prison in 2023, even he still doesn’t have a grasp of how much Holmes is deceiving people, or what she actually believes. He talked about it in a recent interview, and it both makes things clearer and more opaque at the same time, just like the movie.

In the documentary, Fielder dances around how he feels about Holmes’ statements, like being incredulous when she claims that she’s never lied about anything at all in her life. By design, he rarely calls Holmes on her lies (with a couple of exceptions). He also doesn’t get into the definition of the truth. He leaves that up to us as the audience. Specifically, he doesn’t address whether Holmes even knows if she is lying or not. He addressed this with Wired recently, saying:

It almost feels, at times, that it’s not so black-and-white what’s going on in her head. A lie, a classic lie, is someone who’s like, ‘OK, I am saying something that I’m consciously knowing is not true in this moment.’ But it’s not just the words, it’s the design of every aspect of her life that feels like a part of what is going on.

He also doesn’t quite have his head around just how much of her whole life is wrapped up in the deceit? He adds:

What’s interesting about her to me, I think, just goes beyond that in any given moment … I can’t piece it together. She makes these claims that are like—how could anyone believe this or say they’ve never done this? Is it a lie in that moment? Is it a lie if she believes it to be true?

This is something that has long been discussed and pontificated upon when it comes to the truth and people who spend their loves deceiving people. Do dishonest people like Holmes either know they are lying, or are they so calculating that almost everything becomes a lie, or at minimum a tall tale? Fielder doesn’t seem to have any answers, even after spending all that time with Holmes, as she told him those stories.

One of the most impressive things about You Can See Everything, which is still tearing up the box office on the 2026 movie schedule. is that the movie lives on in the viewers' brains for days or weeks after seeing it. I mean, I saw this movie a month ago, and I still think about it and want to talk about it all the time. Like lies, when you have to peel layers off of them like an onion to get to the truth, this film is much the same way. To mix metaphors, every thread you tug on pulls out more layers to peel back.

#3763. God of War: Ragnarok is reportedly the highest-earning PlayStation Studios game this generation, but Marvel's Spider-Man 2 isn't far behind

God of War: Ragnarok is the generation's best-selling and highest-earning PlayStation Studios game, according to a new report, but the full top 10 list has a few nice surprises.

In the four years since its PS5 release and two years since its PC port, God of War: Ragnarok has reportedly sold just over 20m copies and generated $1.4b in revenue, according to estimates from Alinea Analytics. About 27.5 percent of the 15m copies it sold on console came from physical editions, and the action blockbuster apparently sold a further 1.1m this year alone. Not bad, boy.

Those stats should bode well for the series' next romp God of War: Laufey - which sees Faye take the spotlight across a multi-mythological afterlife and was recently delayed into May 2027 - even if PlayStation moves away from PC ports for its signature single-player games.

Kratos and Atreus only narrowly beat out perhaps the biggest superhero of them all: Marvel's Spider-Man 2, a game that reportedly made a whopping $1.3b off 19.1m copies across PS5 and PC. The Spidey sequel should keep swinging even higher as the years chug on, though - the report states that sales always surge during the holiday months, and this year's big screen behemoth Spider-Man: Brand New Day led to an even bigger spike than usual.

Racing sim royalty Gran Turismo 7 ($841m), bug-squashing phenomenon Helldivers 2 ($786m), robo-dino sequel Horizon: Forbidden West ($485m), vengeful spirit sim Ghost of Yotei ($410m), undead remake The Last of Us Part 1 ($341m), multidimensional romp Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart ($334m), Stellar Blade ($316m) and delightful throwback Astro Bot ($292m) round out the top 10 games published by PlayStation Studios this generation.

It's worth noting that Helldivers 2 and Stellar Blade were developed by studios outside the PlayStation umbrella, but the console maker still published both upon release. Ghost of Yotei's performance is also particularly impressive since Sucker Punch's sequel has only been out for a year and didn't get the benefit of a PC port, like many of its PS5 siblings. The success couldn't save Sucker Punch from recent layoffs, however.

On PlayStation's decision to kill disc-based physical releases, analyst Rhys Elliott said that the bottom five games in the list together made $281.7m this year alone: "PlayStation wants those numbers to be bigger in the coming years, which is one of the reasons it's killing the disc (alongside the better margins it and publishers get through digital.)"

The dust hasn't even settled yet after Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO, and the US government is already making it pretty clear where it stands on who gets the job next.

Nvidia CFO Colette Kress has taken up the role of CEO following Huang's departure, but only on an interim basis. The Nvidia board will have to decide on a full-time replacement to take over from Huang, who had led the company since its founding in 1993.

The chairman of the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, John Moolenaar, has put out a statement on the high-profile departure. It reads:

“Jensen Huang’s firing from the company he founded is an unfortunate end that could have been avoided."

"It is in our national interest for Nvidia and our other AI champions to succeed, but American companies should never jeopardize our nation’s security by giving Chinese companies access to their most advanced chips. Nvidia must now change its corporate practices and appoint leadership that makes national security its top priority."

Moolenaar also says that Congress should aim to increase control over exports of top AI chips to China, with further export control legislation in the national defense bill by the end of the year.

Some in the US government are more opposed to China than others, and the China committee most among them.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

Currently, Nvidia is allowed to sell its second-best AI chips to China, the H200, with the Commerce Department picking up a fee for rubber-stamping any applications by Chinese companies for them.

That's been a contentious approach, with a recent report stating some cards may be landing in the hands of companies with dubious operations. Though clearly trying to totally block sales doesn't always work either, as chip smuggling is an issue.

To add to that, the Chinese Communist Party may not even want the chips heading to companies in the country. Reports suggest many are stuck in Hong Kong, waiting to be released, and they dilly-dallied for a while on agreeing to import them in the first place.

Additionally, when attempting to change your email addresses, no verification is sent to the old email address, with information only being directed toward the newly inputted email account. Beyond security issues, many have complained about a host of features previously on the site being removed or obfuscated in the shift to “vibe-coded brainrot.” Some have noticed that there’s no longer differentiation between redeemed and unredeemed games and codes, making it harder for users with large libraries to sort through their purchase history and find unclaimed games. For now, itâs recommended to remove any payment information saved to your Humble account in case of unauthorized access, at least until these issues are resolved. Since its debut in the mid-'90s, Friends has permeated various parts of pop culture and is still considered one of the best sitcoms of all time. Between the hilarious one-liners and memorable storylines, there is a lot to love. In fact, it made such an impact that women flocked to hair salons to get “The Rachel” haircut to mirror Jennifer Aniston’s beloved character. It seems like the ‘do is making a comeback, and while I don’t know how to feel about it, Aniston shared some thoughts.

Rachel Green’s iconic haircut, dubbed “The Rachel,” is a shoulder-length bouncy bob with layers. And even though it may seem like a lot, essentially every woman in the ‘90s wanted to have that same haircut. While the term "viral" wasn't really a thing at that point, that's now the best way to describe the craze. The haircut has now made its way to the 21st Century, as Gen Z has apparently found a love for it. Now, with a modern version of The Rachel making the rounds, with longer and softer layers, Aniston opened up to Elle about its return:

I love that people are still inspired by it. The modern versions feel a little more relaxed and lived-in, which I love.

I have mixed feelings on this. At this point, it feels kind of late for The Rachel to be going viral. It’s a ‘90s haircut, and it should stay in the ‘90s, even if there's a modern version. On the other hand, I do love that Aniston is all for the comeback and appreciates that the younger generation is jumping on the bandwagon. Of course, there have been plenty of ‘90s outfits and trends that have come back, so it probably shouldn't be too surprising that this 'do is one of them.

That being said, despite the look’s longevity for the past 30 years, Aniston was not exactly a fan of it back in the day. Rachel’s haircut may have seemed effortless and amazing, but the actress recalled that getting it together was easier said than done:

I remember how much work that original haircut was!

Considering how great Rachel’s hair looked throughout all seasons of Friends, I’m not surprised to know that it took some time to get it looking the way it did. Still, given the fact that The Rachel has been a consistent favorite over the years, it seems people don’t mind putting in the work to keep it up. It's funny to think about how nostalgia can influence different parts of our daily lives.

At present, what I wonder is whether 30 years from now, The Rachel will still be a hit. It’s hard to predict what fashion will look like in three decades or even in one, to be honest. However, if Friends continues to remain in the zeitgeist, which I’m sure will be the case, I wouldn’t be surprised if another version of the hairstyle comes along and fits with the times. For now, fans can see the look in all its glory by streaming Friends with an HBO Max subscription.

#3757. "Something's really possible" - Mass Effect cast rally around efforts to save the franchise on the first N7 Day after BioWare's closure

I'm Commander Shepard and this is my favorite video on the internet.

This N7 Day was the first without developer BioWare around, but fans of the Mass Effect series didn't let 7th November go by quietly. The community managed to get several notable Mass Effect actors to lend their voice to the increasingly loud 'SaveMassEffect' movement.

In the weeks since BioWare's shock closure and Mass Effect Universe's cancellation, the community-organised We Are Mass Effect group have put up billboards in Times Square, a mobile billboard outside BioWare Edmonton's former office and much more while directing attention to an online petition.

Today is a very special day for Mass Effect fans. We've worked incredibly hard to bring together most of the original Mass Effect trilogy's voice cast to share a very important message with you. We need to #SaveMassEffect. https://t.co/FOp0qp4wBI

And for the series' annual celebration, the group managed to get a sizable portion of the Mass Effect cast to join in. Commander Shepard actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, original trilogy composer Sam Hulick, Garrus' Brandon Keener, Jack's Courtnay Taylor, Tali'Zorah's Ash Sroka, Thane's Keythe Farley and many more all showed up in a two-minute video to help potentially salvage the series - sometimes in character.

"When we heard about the formal closing of Boware, I felt weirdly hopeful," Hale said in a separate interview with IGN. "I can't explain it. I just got so weirdly hopeful. My first thought, of course, was for the devs and all the people. And then I just closed my eyes and crossed my fingers and I said, 'I feel something's possible. You know, something's really possible.'"

The other half of Commander Shepard, Mark Meer, noted that "this didn't all just happen in the last 10 days." Near yearly layoffs at EA had slowly trimmed multiple BioWare teams down, sometimes even affecting studio veterans who had been at the company for decades.

#3754. GTA 6 pre-orders are tracking "well above expectations" and the game will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two, says CEO Strauss Zelnick

Today, as part of Take-Two Interactive Software's Q2 2027 earnings call, Strauss Zelnick noted that pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto 6 are tracking "far above expectations", and is certain that soon "numbers will speak for themselves" when it comes to the game.

Zelnick also promised GTA Online and GTA 5 will continue to receive updates in order to support the "nearly 235 million" units sold to date across "an unprecedented three console generations". The GTA series as a whole has, to date, sold over 480 million units. Karl Statoff, president at Take-Two, adds the launch of GTA 6 will be a "defining moment for the company and global entertainment industry". Zelnick adds, later in a question and answer session, that he expects GTA 6 to "set a new baseline" for Take-Two. "The future's really bright across the board," he notes.

For the next quarter, Take-Two expects to deliver $3.35 billion to $3.5 billion - with "recurrent consumer spending" to raise by 12 percent, driven by "the groundbreaking release" of Grand Theft Auto 6, and expects to see "significant growth for the Grand Theft Auto series", driven by sales of - specifically - Grand Theft Auto 6's Ultimate Edition, which includes add-on content, and that most people are pre-ordering at its $100 price point. That bonus $20 between the $80 base edition and the Ultimate Edition is counted as "recurrent consumer spending", as is part of that massive bump the company has seen.

It also seems that we will see more GTA games - or content, at least - sooner than expected. "We do think that the nature and velocity of the content we'll see from our iconic franchises, including GTA, will look dramatically different over the next decade." It's a vague comment, but assumedly the work done on the engine and backend of GTA 6 means we'll see more content arriving in shorter order than we're used to for the series. This is per an article published by IGN in line with the earning's call going live.

Elsewhere in the earnings call, Take-Two referred to its current setup with its mobile, sports, 'core new IP' and 'core existing IP' as "the strongest development pipeline in the company's history". In terms of new IP, Zelnick directed investors to consider the launches of incoming projects like Ken Levine's mysterious Judas and Project Ethos (which we don't know too much about yet, other than it's billed as a "roguelike hero shooter"). For core IP, 8 sequels and 7 remakes, remasters, and platform extensions.

Buoyed by these plans, Zelnick outlines that he believes that fiscal year 2027 "will be a historic year for Take-Two" as the company is buoyed by "recent and upcoming releases". No prizes for what that's referring to. If you're curious about what sort of numbers we may be looking at here, all you need to do is cast your mind back to 2014, where you will remember GTA 5 made $1bn in just three days.

Robert Pattinson is living out a real-life ‘pinch me’ moment, and it has nothing to do with Batman. The actor has always wanted to work with Denzel Washington, who is one of his acting heroes. Well, that dream is coming true, because Washington and Pattinson are doing a movie together. However, there is one thing that surprised the Dune star.

Pattinson's first movie of the 2027 movie schedule, The Take, was an easy yes thanks to a “dream-team situation,” partnering him with one of the greatest actors of all time. The Primetime actor dished with Entertainment Weekly about what caught him off guard (in the best way) while working with Washington:

Denzel is one of the reasons I wanted to become an actor, so getting to work with him was pretty incredible. What I loved was seeing how alive the material is for him. Even after all these years of acting, he’s still looking for something new in every take. I also didn’t realize how much he liked to improvise, which made it all the more exciting. You’d start a five-page scene thinking you knew where it was going, and then suddenly you’re completely off-piste. It was really thrilling.

Sounds like Pattinson had to stay on his toes just as much as his character, Noah, who is recruited by “a charismatic thief” (aka Denzel Washington) to rob Manhattan’s richest bank. To make things more complicated, this is also the bank where his girlfriend (played by Daisy Edgar-Jones) works as a teller. The movie’s official synopsis teases that “a bank guard, a teller, and a master thief get caught in a deadly game of cons and double crosses.” This is definitely up the actor’s alley, as he tends to lean toward twisty movies, such as Primetime about To Catch A Predator host Chris Hansen.

However, this movie sounds less polarizing and more thrilling. I’m sure some of that improv worked in Pattinson’s favor given the movie’s dynamics. It’s being described as a mix of a heist film and psychological drama, and promises to keep you surprised until the end. In fact, director Fernando Meirelles assures that even the last 10 seconds are important. Part of the excitement of the movie is being credited to Washington. Meirelles backs Pattinson’s statements and shares how easy improvising is for The Equalizer actor:

He constantly surprises you. Sometimes, when I ask him where a particular line came from, he’ll simply say, ‘I have no idea.’ There are quite a few of those moments in the final cut.

While the movie is strictly from Pattinson’s POV, it sounds like Washington is going to be a scene-stealer. However, while Washington is getting rave reviews from his coworkers, the director also made sure to shout out Pattinson, calling him “one of the best actors working today.” This is definitely true, given the actor has released three movies this year and still has Dune: Part 3 set to hit the 2026 schedule on December 18. He certainly doesn’t seem to be slowing down, and I wonder if Washington gave him any advice on working so much.

Though this full-circle moment with the Gladiator II actor had to be a highlight, given Pattinson previously worked with Denzel's son John David Washington in Christopher Nolan’s Tenet. Maybe one day the three of them can do a project together. Perhaps something just as ‘puzzling’ as The Take and with just as much improvising.

Hopefully, when the movie comes out on January 15, 2027, they’ll share what lines were improvised, because I’m dying to know. At least, I’ll be able to watch it with a Netflix subscription.

#3752. Naughty Dog’s Intergalactic is ‘at the last stage of production,’ Neil Druckmann says

Druckmann finally reveals some new details for Naughty Dog's next game.

Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is Naughty Dog’s latest game, but aside from a few teasers, we haven’t really seen much of the game at all. Despite the clandestine approach, the game is actually “at the last stage of production,” according to Naughty Dog’s chief Neil Druckmann.

Speaking on Revenge Of’s Comic Creators Block Party podcast, Druckmann said Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is “at the last stage of production,” where “we can play it, and we’re refining and polishing it,” but did not reveal too many details about the game’s plot or setting outside of saying it’s Naughty Dog’s venture into science fiction.

Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet is in the final stage of production according to Neil Druckmann.He describes it as a combination of Jak and Daxter, Uncharted, and The Last of Us:"We used to have another game franchise called Jak & Daxter […] And with this one, we really…

The choice of sci-fi as the setting came from a desire to build something less grounded and more epic in scale, which, as Druckmann explains, wasn’t really possible with The Last of Us and Uncharted. However, the director said some TLOU and Uncharted DNA definitely went into the creation of Intergalactic, with that game being “a combination” of Jack & Dexter and these two mentioned IPs. Specifically, Druckmann says the studio took Uncharted‘s pulp action, TLOU‘s drama, and Jack & Dexter‘s science-fantasy and smashed them together to form this new and exciting adventure.

“We really wanted to expand our deep gameplay systems. Like, can we sustain the kind of cinematic storytelling we’re used to telling and go even deeper with gameplay,”

“We really wanted to expand our deep gameplay systems. Like, can we sustain the kind of cinematic storytelling we’re used to telling and go even deeper with gameplay?” Druckmann said.

Anime played a crucial role as inspiration for Intergalactic, the director said, naming Evangelion and Akira as key examples, and not just because of their futuristic style. Both of these anime have intricate and complex philosophical ideas which are approached in a very strange, disconnected, and weird way, or, as Druckmann puts it, they take you on a “wild ride,” and that is exactly what Naughty Dog aims to do in Intergalactic.

Druckmann added that the studio plans to reveal more of the story and the gameplay for Intergalactic next year, and that players will be surprised to see what the game is actually about.
